docString: A diagonal Berry connection is real, expressed as vanishing imaginary part.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} [inst_3 : Fintype ι] {κ : Type u_3} (data : BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData κ ι H)
  [inst_4 : DecidableEq ι] (μ ν : κ) (n : ι),
  (∀ (ρ : κ), IsSelfAdjoint (data.hamiltonianDerivative ρ)) →
    (∀ (m : ι), m ≠ n → data.energy m ≠ data.energy n) →
      data.berryCurvature μ ν n =
        ∑ m,
          if m = n then 0
          else
            2 *
              (data.hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElement μ m n / ↑(data.energy n - data.energy m) *
                  (data.hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElement ν n m / ↑(data.energy n - data.energy m))).im
name: BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.berryCurvature_eq_sum_hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElements
docString:
Force/Hamiltonian-derivative matrix-element representation of Berry curvature for a
nondegenerate band.

This is the finite-dimensional pointwise formula needed by the clean anomalous-Hall consumer.
Self-adjointness of all directional Hamiltonian derivatives is an explicit hypothesis.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} [inst_3 : Fintype ι] {κ : Type u_3} (data : BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData κ ι H) (μ ν : κ)
  (n : ι),
  data.berryCurvature μ ν n =
    ∑ m,
      -2 *
        (inner ℂ (data.eigenvectorDerivative μ n) (data.eigenbasis m) *
            inner ℂ (data.eigenbasis m) (data.eigenvectorDerivative ν n)).im
name: BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.berryCurvature_eq_sum_innerProducts
docString:
Completeness of the finite orthonormal eigenbasis expands the derivative-state curvature into
band-resolved inner-product terms.

statement:

  {ι : Type u_2} [inst_3 : Fintype ι] {κ : Type u_3} (data : BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData κ ι H) (μ ν : κ)
  (n : ι), data.berryCurvature ν μ n = -data.berryCurvature μ ν n
name: BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.berryCurvature_swap
docString: Berry curvature is antisymmetric in its two parameter directions.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} [inst_3 : Fintype ι] {κ : Type u_3} (data : BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData κ ι H) (μ : κ)
  {m n : ι},
  m ≠ n →
    data.energy m ≠ data.energy n →
      data.berryConnection μ m n =
        Complex.I * data.hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElement μ m n / ↑(data.energy n - data.energy m)
name: BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.bornFock_berryConnection
docString: Born--Fock formula in Berry-connection form.

statement:

  {m n : ι},
  m ≠ n →
    data.energy m ≠ data.energy n →
      inner ℂ (data.eigenbasis m) (data.eigenvectorDerivative μ n) =
        data.hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElement μ m n / ↑(data.energy n - data.energy m)
name: BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.bornFock_inner
docString:
Born--Fock off-diagonal eigenvector-derivative formula in parameter direction `μ`.

The nondegeneracy needed for division by the level spacing is an explicit theorem hypothesis rather
than a global restriction on `PointwiseEigenbasisData`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} [inst_3 : Fintype ι] {κ : Type u_3} (data : BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData κ ι H) (μ ν : κ),
  IsSelfAdjoint (data.hamiltonianDerivative μ) →
    IsSelfAdjoint (data.hamiltonianDerivative ν) →
      ∀ {m n : ι},
        m ≠ n →
          data.energy m ≠ data.energy n →
            -2 *
                (inner ℂ (data.eigenvectorDerivative μ n) (data.eigenbasis m) *
                    inner ℂ (data.eigenbasis m) (data.eigenvectorDerivative ν n)).im =
              2 *
                (data.hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElement μ m n / ↑(data.energy n - data.energy m) *
                    (data.hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElement ν n m / ↑(data.energy n - data.energy m))).im
name: BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.curvatureInnerTerm_eq_hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElements
docString:
An off-diagonal completeness term equals the conventional force-matrix Berry-curvature term.
The two real level-spacing factors are intentionally kept separate here; a downstream consumer may
normalize them to a squared denominator if desired.

ambient pairing agrees with selecting the corresponding endpoint of the decomposed normalized
pair.

  ∏ pr ∈ pairing.pairs, f pr =

      ∏ pr ∈ pairing.eraseZeroPair.pairs, f (↑(pairing.eraseZeroOrderIso pr.1), ↑(pairing.eraseZeroOrderIso pr.2))

statement:

  (global : Combinatorics.Pairing n) (componentPairing : (B : ι) → Combinatorics.Pairing (m B))
  (componentPairEquiv : (B : ι) × (componentPairing B).NormalizedPair ≃ global.NormalizedPair)
  (pairValue : Fin (2 * n) → Fin (2 * n) → R) (localPairValue : (B : ι) → Fin (2 * m B) → Fin (2 * m B) → R),
  (∀ (B : ι) (pr : (componentPairing B).NormalizedPair),
      pairValue (↑(componentPairEquiv ⟨B, pr⟩)).1 (↑(componentPairEquiv ⟨B, pr⟩)).2 =
        localPairValue B (↑pr).1 (↑pr).2) →
    ∏ pr ∈ global.pairs, pairValue pr.1 pr.2 = ∏ B, ∏ pr ∈ (componentPairing B).pairs, localPairValue B pr.1 pr.2

statement:
∀ {a b n : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommMonoid R] (e : Combinatorics.PositionSplitting a b n)
  (P : Combinatorics.Pairing a) (Q : Combinatorics.Pairing b) (value : Fin (2 * n) → Fin (2 * n) → R)
  (leftValue : Fin (2 * a) → Fin (2 * a) → R) (rightValue : Fin (2 * b) → Fin (2 * b) → R),
  (∀ (pr : P.NormalizedPair),
      value (↑((Combinatorics.Pairing.ofSplitNormalizedPairEquiv e P Q) (Sum.inl pr))).1
          (↑((Combinatorics.Pairing.ofSplitNormalizedPairEquiv e P Q) (Sum.inl pr))).2 =
        leftValue (↑pr).1 (↑pr).2) →
    (∀ (pr : Q.NormalizedPair),
        value (↑((Combinatorics.Pairing.ofSplitNormalizedPairEquiv e P Q) (Sum.inr pr))).1
            (↑((Combinatorics.Pairing.ofSplitNormalizedPairEquiv e P Q) (Sum.inr pr))).2 =
          rightValue (↑pr).1 (↑pr).2) →
      ∏ pr ∈ (Combinatorics.Pairing.ofSplit e P Q).pairs, value pr.1 pr.2 =
        (∏ pr ∈ P.pairs, leftValue pr.1 pr.2) * ∏ pr ∈ Q.pairs, rightValue pr.1 pr.2

docString:
The contraction product of a pairing reassembled from two independent parts splits into
two local contraction products when the corresponding normalized pair values agree.

The slot splitting need not preserve the linear order of positions. The hypotheses refer to
the *normalized ambient pairs* given by `ofSplitNormalizedPairEquiv`, so that any reversal
of a transported pair is handled by the local kernel comparison rather than silently dropped.

statement:

        (-1) ^ pairing.crossingCount

docString:

`pairing`, each in either endpoint order, its sign is `-1` to the number of reversed blocks times
`-1` to `pairing`'s crossing count.

docString:
If the factorial-normalized moments of a unit-constant formal power series are the normalized
object moments of a multiplicative connected decomposition, its formal-log coefficients are exactly
the connected-object contributions.

name: Combinatorics.factorial_mul_coeff_logOf_eq_connectedContribution_replica
docString:
Replica-method form of the generic formal linked-cluster theorem.  If the
factorial-normalized coefficients of a unit-constant formal power series are the object moments of
a multiplicative connected decomposition, then the factorial-normalized formal-log coefficient is
the connected contribution.  The proof factors through the equality of the two replica
polynomials, not through cumulant inversion.

      s ≠ ∅ →
        ↑s.card.factorial * (PowerSeries.coeff s.card) Z.logOf =
          Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment (fun T => ↑T.card.factorial * (PowerSeries.coeff T.card) Z) s
name: Combinatorics.factorial_mul_coeff_logOf_eq_cumulantFromMoment
docString:
Factorial-normalized coefficients of `logOf Z` are the finite-set cumulants of the
factorial-normalized coefficients of `Z`.

docString:
After normalization by any nonzero constant coefficient, factorial-normalized formal-log
coefficients are the finite-set cumulants of the normalized coefficients.

      (∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ s, a ≠ b → f a b + f b a ≡ g a b [MOD n]) →

An ordering selects one representative from each unordered pair in an off-diagonal sum.

If the combined contribution of each pair agrees modulo `n` with `g a b`, then the sum of `f` over
all ordered distinct pairs agrees with the sum of `g` in the orientation selected by an injective
order.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] (ζ : R),
  ζ * ζ = 1 →
    ∀ (moment : (n : ℕ) → (Fin (2 * n) → α) → R) (pairValue : α → α → R)
      (Admissible : (n : ℕ) → (Fin (2 * n) → α) → Prop),
      (∀ (C : Fin 0 → α), moment 0 C = 1) →
        (∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * (n + 1)) → α),
            Admissible (n + 1) C → ∀ (j : Fin (2 * n + 1)), Admissible n fun i => C (j.succAbove i).succ) →
          (∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * (n + 1)) → α),
              Admissible (n + 1) C →
                moment (n + 1) C =
                  ∑ j, ζ ^ ↑j * pairValue (C 0) (C j.succ) * moment n fun i => C (j.succAbove i).succ) →
            ∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * n) → α),
              Admissible n C → moment n C = ∑ P, ζ ^ P.crossingCount * ∏ pr ∈ P.pairs, pairValue (C pr.1) (C pr.2)
name: Combinatorics.moment_eq_pairing_sum_of_first_pair_recursion
docString: The abstract first-pair recursion.

    right.1 < right.2 →
      left.1 ≠ right.1 →
        left.1 ≠ right.2 →
          left.2 ≠ right.1 →

statement:
∀ {m : ℕ} {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (ζ : R),
  ζ * ζ = 1 →
    ∀ (e : Combinatorics.SideSplitting m) (pv : Fin (2 * m) → Fin (2 * m) → R),
      (∀ (i i' : Fin m), pv (e (Sum.inl i)) (e (Sum.inl i')) = 0) →
        Combinatorics.pairingSum ζ pv =
          Combinatorics.sideSplittingWeight ζ e *
            Combinatorics.permutationSum ζ (Combinatorics.exchangeMatrix ζ e pv) Finset.univ
name: Combinatorics.pairingSum_eq_permutationSum_of_inl_vanishing
docString:
**Generic exchange-statistics reduction.** If the pair value vanishes on two left-side
positions, the crossing-weighted pairing sum reduces to the cycle-weighted permutation sum of the
side-oriented matrix, up to the factor fixed by the side splitting. The involutive hypothesis is
needed only to identify crossing parity with permutation cycle parity.

statement:

  ζ ≠ 0 →
    Combinatorics.permutationConnectedCycleSeries ζ (Matrix.diagonal w) =
      -ζ⁻¹ • ∑ i, (PowerSeries.rescale (-ζ * w i)) (PowerSeries.log ℂ)
name: Combinatorics.permutationConnectedCycleSeries_diagonal_eq_neg_inv_smul_sum_log
docString:
For a diagonal kernel and nonzero exchange weight, the connected-cycle series is the scaled sum
of the modewise formal logarithms `log(1 - ζ wᵢ t)`.

statement:

name: Combinatorics.permutationSum_eq_momentFromCumulant
docString: The arbitrary-`ζ` permutation sum is the moment transform of the single-cycle contribution.

statement:

name: Combinatorics.permutationSum_univ_eq_sum_perm
docString:
On the full finite index type, the connected-decomposition backend is the usual direct sum over
all permutations with weight `ζ ^ cycleDefect`. This is the bridge consumed by the perfect-pairing
reduction; it is not a second backend.

name: Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentSetFunction_eq_iff
docString:
Equality of the bundled power-series moment function with normalized finite-set moment data is
equivalent to equality of the factorial-normalized coefficients on every finite set.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : Field R] [CharZero R] {Z : PowerSeries R},
  PowerSeries.constantCoeff Z = 1 →
    ∀ (s : Finset α) (k : ℕ),
      ↑s.card.factorial / ↑k.factorial * (PowerSeries.coeff s.card) ((Z - 1) ^ k) =
        ∑ π, Finpartition.partitionProduct (fun T => ↑T.card.factorial * (PowerSeries.coeff T.card) Z) ↑π
name: Combinatorics.replicaCoeffPolynomial_descPochhammerCoeff_eq_fixedBlockMomentSum
docString:
The falling-factorial coefficient in the power-series replica polynomial is the sum of
products of factorial-normalized moments over set partitions with the corresponding number of
blocks.

statement:

  PowerSeries.constantCoeff Z = 1 →
    ∀ (κ : Finset α → R) (s : Finset α),
      (∀ (T : Finset α), ↑T.card.factorial * (PowerSeries.coeff T.card) Z = Finpartition.momentFromCumulant κ T) →
        Z.replicaCoeffPolynomial s.card = Finpartition.replicaPolynomial κ s
name: Combinatorics.replicaCoeffPolynomial_eq_replicaPolynomial
docString:
Under the forward finite-set moment relation, the fixed-order power-series replica polynomial
is exactly the finite-set replica polynomial.  This is the algebraic bridge between the two replica
constructions and uses no moment-cumulant inversion.

statement:

kernel-dependent contribution.

docString:
On the full finite index type, the connected contribution is the direct sum over permutations
that are a single cycle on the whole type, with the universal connected-cycle weight.

docString:
Division-free formal trace-log identity for arbitrary exchange weight.

Multiplying the connected-cycle series by `ζ` gives the negative coefficientwise trace-log

  [inst_4 : _root_.Module 𝕜 OneForm] [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid Obs] [inst_6 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Obs]
  {d : Test →ₗ[𝕜] OneForm} {Φ : Test →ₗ[𝕜] Obs} {J : OneForm →ₗ[𝕜] Obs},
  ConservationLaw.IsDifferentialCurrent d Φ J → ConservationLaw.DependsOnlyOnDifferential d Φ
name: ConservationLaw.IsDifferentialCurrent.dependsOnlyOnDifferential
docString:
Choosing a differential current implies the representation-independent statement that transport
depends only on differential data.

statement:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {Test : Type u_2} {OneForm : Type u_3} {Obs : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring 𝕜]
  [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid Test] [inst_2 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Test] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid OneForm]

  {d : Test →ₗ[𝕜] OneForm} {Φ : Test →ₗ[𝕜] Obs} {J : OneForm →ₗ[𝕜] Obs},
  ConservationLaw.IsDifferentialCurrent d Φ J → ∀ {f : Test}, d f = 0 → Φ f = 0
name: ConservationLaw.IsDifferentialCurrent.eq_zero_of_map_eq_zero
docString: A factorized transport functional vanishes on test objects annihilated by `d`.

statement:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {Test : Type u_2} {OneForm : Type u_3} {Obs : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring 𝕜]
  [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid Test] [inst_2 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Test] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid OneForm]
  [inst_4 : _root_.Module 𝕜 OneForm] [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid Obs] [inst_6 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Obs]

  ConservationLaw.IsDifferentialCurrent d Φ J ↔ Φ = J ∘ₗ d
name: ConservationLaw.IsDifferentialCurrent.iff_eq_comp
docString: Factorization through `d` is equivalent to equality with the composite `J ∘ d`.

statement:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {Test : Type u_2} {OneForm : Type u_3} {Obs : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring 𝕜]
  [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid Test] [inst_2 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Test] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid OneForm]
  [inst_4 : _root_.Module 𝕜 OneForm] [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid Obs] [inst_6 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Obs]
  {d : Test →ₗ[𝕜] OneForm} {Φ : Test →ₗ[𝕜] Obs} {J₁ J₂ : OneForm →ₗ[𝕜] Obs},
  ConservationLaw.IsDifferentialCurrent d Φ J₁ →
    ConservationLaw.DifferentialCurrentEquivalent d J₁ J₂ → ConservationLaw.IsDifferentialCurrent d Φ J₂
name: ConservationLaw.IsDifferentialCurrent.of_currentEquivalent
docString: Being a differential current is invariant under differential-current equivalence.

statement:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {Test : Type u_2} {OneForm : Type u_3} {Obs : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring 𝕜]
  [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid Test] [inst_2 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Test] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid OneForm]

  ConservationLaw.IsDifferentialCurrent d Φ J →
    ∀ (L : Obs →ₗ[𝕜] Obs'), ConservationLaw.IsDifferentialCurrent d (L ∘ₗ Φ) (L ∘ₗ J)
name: ConservationLaw.IsDifferentialCurrent.postcomp
docString: Postcomposition by a linear observable map preserves a differential factorization.

statement:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {Test : Type u_2} {OneForm : Type u_3} {Obs : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring 𝕜]
  [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid Test] [inst_2 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Test] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid OneForm]
  [inst_4 : _root_.Module 𝕜 OneForm] [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid Obs] [inst_6 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Obs]

name: ConservationLaw.IsDifferentialCurrent.smul
docString: Scalar multiplication preserves a differential factorization.

statement:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {Test : Type u_2} {OneForm : Type u_3} {Obs : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring 𝕜]
  [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid Test] [inst_2 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Test] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid OneForm]

docString:
Any two densities representing the same transport functional are weakly equivalent on exact
test 1-forms.

name: ConservationLaw.LocalCurrentDensityRepresentation.isCurrentDensity
docString: Proof that `currentDensity` represents the transport through the supplied pairing.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  ((LieAlgebra.ad ℂ (Module.End ℂ V)) h) ((ConservationLaw.localizedQuantityFunctional V M m) f) =
    (ConservationLaw.transportFunctional V h M m) f + (ConservationLaw.sourceFunctional V h M m) f
name: ConservationLaw.ad_localizedQuantityFunctional
docString: The packaged localized quantity satisfies the same transport/source decomposition.

statement: ∀ {a b : ℝ} {f : ℝ → ℝ}, tsupport f ⊆ Set.Ioo a b → f a = 0 ∧ f b = 0
name: ConservationLaw.endpoint_values_eq_zero_of_tsupport_subset_Ioo
docString:
A function whose topological support is strictly inside an interval vanishes at both
endpoints.

statement: ∀ {a b : ℝ} {f g : ℝ → ℝ}, tsupport f ⊆ Set.Ioo a b → ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, deriv f x * g x = ∫ (x : ℝ), deriv f x * g x
name: ConservationLaw.integral_deriv_mul_eq_integral_of_tsupport_subset_Ioo
docString:
The derivative of a function supported strictly inside an interval has the same support
window for the purpose of multiplying by an arbitrary function.

statement: ∀ {a b : ℝ} {f g : ℝ → ℝ}, tsupport f ⊆ Set.Ioo a b → ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, f x * g x = ∫ (x : ℝ), f x * g x
name: ConservationLaw.integral_mul_eq_integral_of_tsupport_subset_Ioo
docString:
A function supported strictly inside an interval makes its product with any function
interval-integrable and whole-space integrable through the interval support theorem.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  ⁅h, ConservationLaw.localizedQuantity V M m f⁆ =
    ConservationLaw.transportCommutator V h M m f + ConservationLaw.sourceCommutator V h M m f
name: ConservationLaw.lie_localizedQuantity
docString: The commutator is a derivation on symmetric localization, giving transport plus source.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  ⁅h, m⁆ = 0 → ⁅h, ConservationLaw.localizedQuantity V M m f⁆ = ConservationLaw.transportCommutator V h M m f
name: ConservationLaw.lie_localizedQuantity_of_commutes
docString: For a conserved quantity, the localized balance identity contains only transport.

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (h A B : W →ₗ[ℂ] W),
  ⁅h, ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A B⁆ =
    ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct ⁅h, A⁆ B + ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A ⁅h, B⁆
name: ConservationLaw.lie_symmetrizedProduct
docString: The commutator acts as a derivation on the symmetrized product.

statement:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {Test : Type u_2} {OneForm : Type u_3} {Obs : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring 𝕜]
  [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid Test] [inst_2 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Test] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid OneForm]
  [inst_4 : _root_.Module 𝕜 OneForm] [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid Obs] [inst_6 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Obs]
  {CurrentDensity : Type u_5} [inst_7 : AddCommMonoid CurrentDensity] [inst_8 : _root_.Module 𝕜 CurrentDensity]
  {d : Test →ₗ[𝕜] OneForm} {Φ : Test →ₗ[𝕜] Obs} {pairing : ConservationLaw.LocalCurrentPairing},
  ConservationLaw.SeparatesCurrentDensities d pairing →
    ∀ (R₁ R₂ : ConservationLaw.LocalCurrentDensityRepresentation d Φ pairing), R₁.currentDensity = R₂.currentDensity
name: ConservationLaw.localCurrentDensity_unique_of_separates
docString:
A local current density is unique when the concrete differential tests and pairing separate
current densities.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  (ConservationLaw.localizationCommutatorFunctional V h M) f = ⁅h, M f⁆
name: ConservationLaw.localizationCommutatorFunctional_apply

statement:
∀ {OneForm : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup OneForm] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ OneForm] (V : Type u_2)
  [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (velocity m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (N : OneForm →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
  (α : OneForm), (ConservationLaw.localizationCorrectionCurrentFlux V velocity m N) α = (1 / 4) • ⁅velocity, ⁅N α, m⁆⁆
name: ConservationLaw.localizationCorrectionCurrentFlux_apply

statement:
∀ {OneForm : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup OneForm] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ OneForm] (V : Type u_2)
  [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (velocity m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (N : OneForm →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V),
  (∀ (α : OneForm), ⁅N α, m⁆ = 0) → ConservationLaw.localizationCorrectionCurrentFlux V velocity m N = 0
name: ConservationLaw.localizationCorrectionCurrentFlux_eq_zero_of_commutes
docString: If every supplied localizer commutes with `m`, the localization correction vanishes.

statement:
∀ {OneForm : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup OneForm] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ OneForm] (V : Type u_2)
  [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (velocity : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (N : OneForm →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (q : ℂ),
  ConservationLaw.localizationCorrectionCurrentFlux V velocity (q • LinearMap.id) N = 0
name: ConservationLaw.localizationCorrectionCurrentFlux_smul_id
docString: Charge-like transported quantities `q I` have no localization correction.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  (ConservationLaw.localizedQuantityFunctional V M m) f = ConservationLaw.localizedQuantity V M m f
name: ConservationLaw.localizedQuantityFunctional_apply

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  ⁅M f, m⁆ = 0 → ConservationLaw.localizedQuantity V M m f = M f ∘ₗ m
name: ConservationLaw.localizedQuantity_eq_comp_of_commutes
docString: When localization commutes with the quantity, symmetric localization reduces to `M f ∘ m`.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (q : ℂ) (f : Test),
  ConservationLaw.localizedQuantity V M (q • LinearMap.id) f = q • M f
name: ConservationLaw.localizedQuantity_smul_id
docString: Charge-like quantities `q I` reduce to scalar multiplication under symmetric localization.

statement:
∀ {OneForm : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup OneForm] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ OneForm] (V : Type u_2)
  [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (velocity m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (N : OneForm →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
  (α : OneForm),
  (ConservationLaw.nestedSymmetrizedCurrentFlux V velocity m N) α =
    ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct (N α) velocity) m
name: ConservationLaw.nestedSymmetrizedCurrentFlux_apply

statement:
∀ {OneForm : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup OneForm] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ OneForm] (V : Type u_2)
  [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (velocity m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (N : OneForm →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V),
  ConservationLaw.nestedSymmetrizedCurrentFlux V velocity m N =
    ConservationLaw.symmetrizedCurrentFlux V velocity m N +
      ConservationLaw.localizationCorrectionCurrentFlux V velocity m N
name: ConservationLaw.nestedSymmetrizedCurrentFlux_eq_symmetrized_add_correction
docString: The nested flux is exactly the symmetrized flux plus localization correction.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  ⁅h, m⁆ = 0 → ConservationLaw.sourceCommutator V h M m f = 0
name: ConservationLaw.sourceCommutator_eq_zero_of_commutes
docString: A conserved one-body quantity has no local source/torque contribution.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (q : ℂ) (f : Test),
  ConservationLaw.sourceCommutator V h M (q • LinearMap.id) f = 0
name: ConservationLaw.sourceCommutator_smul_id
docString: Charge-like quantities have no source/torque term.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  (ConservationLaw.sourceFunctional V h M m) f = ConservationLaw.sourceCommutator V h M m f
name: ConservationLaw.sourceFunctional_apply

statement:
∀ {OneForm : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup OneForm] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ OneForm] (V : Type u_2)
  [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (velocity m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (N : OneForm →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
  (α : OneForm),
  (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedCurrentFlux V velocity m N) α =
    ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct (N α) (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct velocity m)
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedCurrentFlux_apply

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (A B : W →ₗ[ℂ] W),
  ((ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProductBilinear W) A) B = ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A B
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProductBilinear_apply

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (A B : W →ₗ[ℂ] W),
  (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProductLeftLinear W A) B = ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A B
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProductLeftLinear_apply

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (B A : W →ₗ[ℂ] W),
  (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProductRightLinear W B) A = ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A B
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProductRightLinear_apply

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (A B : W →ₗ[ℂ] W) (v : W),
  (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A B) v = (1 / 2) • (A (B v) + B (A v))
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct_apply

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (A B : W →ₗ[ℂ] W),
  ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A B = ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct B A
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct_comm
docString: The symmetrized product is symmetric in its two arguments.

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (A B : W →ₗ[ℂ] W),
  ⁅A, B⁆ = 0 → ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A B = A ∘ₗ B
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct_eq_comp_of_commutes
docString: If two operators commute, their symmetrized product reduces to ordinary composition.

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (A v m : W →ₗ[ℂ] W),
  ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A v) m =
    ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct v m) + (1 / 4) • ⁅v, ⁅A, m⁆⁆
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct_nested
docString:
Reassociating two symmetrized products produces a double-commutator correction.

This identity is the representation-independent algebra behind the distinction between a generic
localized transport functional and a current density of the form `1/2 {v,m}`.

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (A v m : W →ₗ[ℂ] W),
  ⁅A, m⁆ = 0 →
    ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A v) m =
      ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct v m)
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct_nested_eq_of_commutes
docString:
If the outer localizer commutes with the transported quantity, nested symmetrization
reassociates without a correction.

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (A : W →ₗ[ℂ] W) (q : ℂ),
  ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A (q • LinearMap.id) = q • A
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct_smul_id
docString: Scalar multiples of the identity behave as scalar quantities under symmetrization.

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (A : W →ₗ[ℂ] W),
  ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct 0 A = 0
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct_zero_left

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (A : W →ₗ[ℂ] W),
  ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A 0 = 0
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct_zero_right

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (q : ℂ) (f : Test),
  ConservationLaw.transportCommutator V h M (q • LinearMap.id) f = q • ⁅h, M f⁆
name: ConservationLaw.transportCommutator_smul_id
docString: Charge-like quantities have transport `q [h,M(f)]`.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  (ConservationLaw.transportFunctional V h M m) f = ConservationLaw.transportCommutator V h M m f
name: ConservationLaw.transportFunctional_apply

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (q : ℂ),
  ConservationLaw.transportFunctional V h M (q • LinearMap.id) =
    q • ConservationLaw.localizationCommutatorFunctional V h M
name: ConservationLaw.transportFunctional_smul_id
docString: For `m = q I`, the transport functional is `q` times the bare localization commutator.

statement:
∀ (a b : ℝ) {test testDerivative current currentDerivative densityTimeDerivative : ℝ → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : ℝ), densityTimeDerivative x + currentDerivative x = 0) →
    (∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt test (testDerivative x) x) →
      (∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt current (currentDerivative x) x) →
        IntervalIntegrable testDerivative MeasureTheory.volume a b →
          IntervalIntegrable currentDerivative MeasureTheory.volume a b →
            ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, test x * densityTimeDerivative x =
              (∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, testDerivative x * current x) - (test b * current b - test a * current a)
name: ConservationLaw.weak_continuity_interval_of_pointwise
docString:
A pointwise one-dimensional conservation equation implies the interval weak balance.

The result is

`∫ test * densityRate = ∫ test' * flux - (test(b) * flux(b) - test(a) * flux(a))`.

statement:
∀ (a b : ℝ) {test testDerivative current currentDerivative densityTimeDerivative : ℝ → ℝ},
  (∀ (x : ℝ), densityTimeDerivative x + currentDerivative x = 0) →
    (∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt test (testDerivative x) x) →
      (∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt current (currentDerivative x) x) →
        IntervalIntegrable testDerivative MeasureTheory.volume a b →

**Only finitely many eigenvalues of a compact self-adjoint operator can exceed any fixed
positive threshold.** Key finiteness step towards countability of `EigenvectorIndex T`: if
infinitely many indices had eigenvalue `≥ ε` in absolute value, the corresponding eigenvectors
would form an orthonormal sequence whose images under `T` stay pairwise at distance `≥ ε√2`,
contradicting compactness of `T` (which forces a norm-convergent, hence Cauchy, subsequence).

lossless real diagonal expectation.

any `x : H`, `T x` is the sum, over `EigenvectorIndex T`, of `T`'s eigenvector expansion of `x`:
`T x = ∑' a, (eigenvalue a : ℂ) • ⟪eigenvectorFamily a, x⟫ • eigenvectorFamily a`. This is the
infinite-dimensional analogue of the finite-dimensional eigenbasis expansions used throughout
`QuantumTheory/Entropy.lean`.

kernel of a compact symmetric operator.

`⟪S, T W⟫_{HS} = ⟪S W†, T⟫_{HS}`.

`summable_inner_adjoint_apply_and_tsum_eq` with the same basis for both arguments identifies
`innerHS d S T` with `Σᵢ ⟪T† dᵢ, S† dᵢ⟫`; applying it again with `d` and `f` swapped identifies

docString:
**Hilbert–Schmidt-ness is preserved by taking the adjoint.** A direct consequence of the
basis-independence computation: `T` being Hilbert–Schmidt with respect to `d` already gives that
`T†` is Hilbert–Schmidt with respect to that *same* `d` (no basis change needed for this
direction).

**Composing a Hilbert–Schmidt operator with a bounded operator on the right stays
Hilbert–Schmidt.** Reduced to the left-composition case via the adjoint identity
`(T * B)† = B† * T†`: `T†` is Hilbert–Schmidt (`isHilbertSchmidt_adjoint`), so `B† * T†` is
Hilbert–Schmidt (`isHilbertSchmidt_comp_left`), so its adjoint `T * B` is Hilbert–Schmidt
(`isHilbertSchmidt_adjoint` again, using `T†† = T`).

  (↑T).IsSymmetric →
    (Module.End.eigenspace (↑T) 0 ⊔
          Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily hT))).topologicalClosure =
      ⊤
name: ContinuousLinearMap.kernel_sup_span_eigenvectorFamily_dense
docString:
**The kernel and `eigenvectorFamily`'s span together are dense.** Their (algebraic) sum
equals the sum of *all* eigenspaces of `T` (over `ℂ`), which is dense by
`orthogonalComplement_iSup_eigenspaces_eq_bot` — since a self-adjoint operator's eigenvalues are
always real, no eigenspace outside `ℝ` (hence outside the kernel-or-nonzero-real split) is ever
missed. The second of the two structural facts combined by
`orthogonal_closure_span_eigenvectorFamily`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsCompactOperator ⇑T),
  (↑T).IsSymmetric →
    (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily hT))).topologicalClosureᗮ =
      Module.End.eigenspace (↑T) 0
name: ContinuousLinearMap.orthogonal_closure_span_eigenvectorFamily
docString:
**The closure of the nonzero-eigenspace part and the kernel are exactly each other's
orthogonal complements.** The key structural fact enabling the `tsum` reconstruction of `T`,
combining `span_eigenvectorFamily_le_kernel_orthogonal` (mutual orthogonality) with
`kernel_sup_span_eigenvectorFamily_dense` (density of their sum).

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H},
  IsCompactOperator ⇑T →
    ∀ (hTpos : T.IsPositive),
      T.HasSummableRealEigenvalues →
        ∀ {ι : Type u_2} {d : ι → H},
          Orthonormal ℂ d →
            (∀ (v : H), ‖v‖ = 1 → 0 < T.diagonalExpectationValue ⋯ v) →
              ∑' (i : ι), T.diagonalExpectationValue ⋯ (d i) = T.spectralTrace → (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range d))ᗮ = ⊥
name: ContinuousLinearMap.orthogonal_span_eq_bot_of_sum_diagonalExpectationValue_eq_spectralTrace
docString:
If a positive operator has strictly positive diagonal value on every unit vector, an
orthonormal family can saturate its spectral trace only when its span has trivial orthogonal
complement.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsCompactOperator ⇑T),
  (↑T).IsSymmetric → Orthonormal ℂ (ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily hT)
name: ContinuousLinearMap.orthonormal_eigenvectorFamily

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsCompactOperator ⇑T),
  Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (ContinuousLinearMap.complexEigenvectorFamily hT)) = ⨆ z, Module.End.eigenspace ↑T ↑z
name: ContinuousLinearMap.span_complexEigenvectorFamily
docString: The span of `complexEigenvectorFamily` is the sum of all nonzero complex eigenspaces.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsCompactOperator ⇑T),
  (↑T).IsSymmetric →
    Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (ContinuousLinearMap.complexEigenvectorFamily hT)) =
      Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily hT))
name: ContinuousLinearMap.span_complexEigenvectorFamily_eq_span_eigenvectorFamily
docString:
For a symmetric operator, the nonzero complex spectral span equals the nonzero real
spectral span.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsCompactOperator ⇑T),
  Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily hT)) = ⨆ μ, Module.End.eigenspace ↑T ↑↑μ
name: ContinuousLinearMap.span_eigenvectorFamily
docString:
The (algebraic) span of `eigenvectorFamily` is exactly the sum of all the nonzero
eigenspaces: each per-eigenspace `stdOrthonormalBasis` spans its own (finite-dimensional)
eigenspace, and these are glued together in the same way as the index type.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsCompactOperator ⇑T),
  (↑T).IsSymmetric →
    Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily hT)) ≤ (Module.End.eigenspace (↑T) 0)ᗮ
name: ContinuousLinearMap.span_eigenvectorFamily_le_kernel_orthogonal
docString:
**`eigenvectorFamily`'s span lies inside the orthogonal complement of the kernel.** Each
eigenvector `eigenvectorFamily hT a` lies in a *nonzero*-eigenvalue eigenspace, which is
orthogonal to the eigenvalue-`0` eigenspace `ker T` (`IsSymmetric.orthogonalFamily_eigenspaces`),
so their span is too. The first of the two structural facts combined by
`orthogonal_closure_span_eigenvectorFamily`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] {T T' : H →L[ℂ] H},
  (↑T).IsSymmetric →
    (↑T').IsSymmetric →
      IsCompactOperator ⇑(T * T') →
        (↑(T * T')).IsSymmetric →
          IsCompactOperator ⇑(T' * T) →
            (↑(T' * T)).IsSymmetric →
              (T * T').HasSummableRealEigenvalues →
                (T' * T).HasSummableRealEigenvalues → (T * T').spectralTrace = (T' * T).spectralTrace
name: ContinuousLinearMap.spectralTrace_comp_comm
docString: Cyclicity of `spectralTrace` for two products satisfying the required hypotheses.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {S : H →L[ℂ] H},
  S.HasSummableRealEigenvalues → Summable fun a => ↑a.fst
name: ContinuousLinearMap.summable_eigenvectorIndex

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} {κ : Type u_3} (d : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (f : HilbertBasis κ ℂ H) (T : H →L[ℂ] H),
  (Summable fun i => ‖T (d i)‖ ^ 2) →
    (Summable fun j => ‖(ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T) (f j)‖ ^ 2) ∧
      ∑' (j : κ), ‖(ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T) (f j)‖ ^ 2 = ∑' (i : ι), ‖T (d i)‖ ^ 2
name: ContinuousLinearMap.summable_norm_sq_adjoint_apply_and_tsum_eq
docString:
**The core basis-independence computation.** If `T` is Hilbert–Schmidt with respect to a
basis `d`, then its adjoint `T†` is Hilbert–Schmidt with respect to *any* basis `f`, with the same
sum of squared norms. This is what makes `IsHilbertSchmidtWrt` (and, applying this twice via
`T†† = T`, comparisons between *any* two bases for `T` itself) basis-independent.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] {ι : Type u_2}
  {κ : Type u_3} (d : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (f : HilbertBasis κ ℂ H) (T : H →L[ℂ] H),
  (Summable fun i => ‖T (d i)‖ ^ 2) →
    (Summable fun j => ‖T (f j)‖ ^ 2) ∧ ∑' (j : κ), ‖T (f j)‖ ^ 2 = ∑' (i : ι), ‖T (d i)‖ ^ 2
name: ContinuousLinearMap.summable_norm_sq_apply_and_tsum_eq
docString:
**The same basis-independence, phrased for `T` itself rather than its adjoint.** Applying
`summable_norm_sq_adjoint_apply_and_tsum_eq` twice — once for `T`, once for `T†` — and using
`T†† = T` transports the sum of squared norms of `T` from any one basis to any other. This
value-level result underlies the canonical basis-independent characterization below.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {S : H →L[ℂ] H},
  (Summable fun a => ↑a.fst) →
    ∑' (a : S.EigenvectorIndex), ↑a.fst =
      ∑' (μ : { ν // ν ≠ 0 }), ↑(Module.finrank ℂ ↥(Module.End.eigenspace ↑S ↑↑μ)) * ↑μ
name: ContinuousLinearMap.tsum_eigenvectorIndex_eq_tsum_mul_finrank
docString:
Splits the spectral-trace `tsum` over `EigenvectorIndex S` into an outer sum over the
base nonzero eigenvalues and an inner finite sum over each eigenspace's basis vectors.

  (∀ (s : ℝ), star (V s) = V s) →
    ∀ (lam : ℂ),

        ∀ {β M t : ℝ},
          0 ≤ β →
            Dyson.ContinuousBoundedInteraction V β M →
              t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β → Dyson.evolution V lam t * star (Dyson.evolution V lam t) = 1
name: Dyson.mul_star_evolution_eq_one_of_star_eq
docString:
A Dyson evolution with self-adjoint interaction and skew-adjoint scalar coupling satisfies
`U(t) U(t)† = 1`.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] {V : ℝ → A} {β M : ℝ},
  Dyson.BoundedInteraction V β M → ∀ (n : ℕ) {τ : ℝ}, τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β → ‖Dyson.coeff V n τ‖ ≤ Dyson.majorant M τ n
name: Dyson.norm_coeff_le_of_bound
docString:
The canonical bounded-interaction hypotheses imply the standard factorial estimate for all
generic Dyson coefficients on `[0, β]`.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] {V : ℝ → A} {β M : ℝ},
  Dyson.BoundedInteraction V β M →
    ∀ (lam : ℂ) {τ : ℝ},
      τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
        ‖Dyson.evolution V lam τ - (1 + Dyson.term V lam τ 1)‖ ≤ ∑' (n : ℕ), Dyson.majorant (‖lam‖ * M) τ (n + 2)
name: Dyson.norm_evolution_sub_one_add_term_one_le_of_bound
docString:
The part of the bounded Dyson evolution beyond first order is controlled by the corresponding
shifted factorial-majorant series.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] {V : ℝ → A} {β M : ℝ},
  Dyson.BoundedInteraction V β M →
    ∀ (lam : ℂ),
      ‖lam‖ ≤ 1 →
        ∀ {τ : ℝ},
          τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
            ‖Dyson.evolution V lam τ - (1 + Dyson.term V lam τ 1)‖ ≤ ‖lam‖ ^ 2 * ∑' (n : ℕ), Dyson.majorant M τ (n + 2)
name: Dyson.norm_evolution_sub_one_add_term_one_le_sq_mul_of_bound
docString:
On the unit coupling ball, the complete Dyson remainder beyond first order is quadratic in the
coupling norm, with an explicit coupling-independent factorial tail.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] {V : ℝ → A} {β M σ : ℝ},
  Dyson.BoundedInteraction V β M →
    σ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β → ∀ (lam : ℂ) (n : ℕ), ‖Dyson.integrand V lam n σ‖ ≤ Dyson.integrandMajorant M β lam n
name: Dyson.norm_integrand_le_of_bound
docString: Uniform pointwise norm control of every generic Volterra-integrand term on `[0, β]`.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] {V : ℝ → A} {β M : ℝ},
  Dyson.BoundedInteraction V β M →
    ∀ (lam : ℂ) (n : ℕ) {τ : ℝ}, τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β → ‖Dyson.term V lam τ n‖ ≤ Dyson.majorant (‖lam‖ * M) τ n
name: Dyson.norm_term_le_of_bound
docString:
The weighted `n`th coefficient is controlled by the factorial majorant with interaction bound
`‖λ‖ M`.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : CStarAlgebra A] {V : ℝ → A},
  (∀ (s : ℝ), star (V s) = V s) →
    ∀ (lam : ℂ),
      star lam = -lam →
        ∀ {β M t : ℝ},
          0 ≤ β →
            Dyson.ContinuousBoundedInteraction V β M →
              t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β → star (Dyson.evolution V lam t) * Dyson.evolution V lam t = 1
name: Dyson.star_mul_evolution_eq_one_of_star_eq
docString:
A Dyson evolution with self-adjoint interaction and skew-adjoint scalar coupling satisfies
`U(t)† U(t) = 1`.

statement: ∀ (M β : ℝ) (lam : ℂ), Summable (Dyson.integrandMajorant M β lam)
name: Dyson.summable_integrandMajorant
docString: The generic Volterra-integrand majorant is summable.

statement: ∀ (M τ : ℝ), Summable (Dyson.majorant M τ)
name: Dyson.summable_majorant
docString: The scalar factorial majorant is summable for every real `M` and `τ`.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] {V : ℝ → A} {β M : ℝ},
  Dyson.BoundedInteraction V β M → ∀ (lam : ℂ) {τ : ℝ}, τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β → Summable (Dyson.term V lam τ)
name: Dyson.summable_term_of_bound
docString: The weighted generic Dyson coefficients are summable at each time in a bounded interval.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (lam : ℂ) (n : ℕ),
  Dyson.term V lam 0 n = if n = 0 then 1 else 0
name: Dyson.term_at_zero
docString: At the initial time, all positive-order weighted coefficients vanish.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (lam : ℂ) (τ : ℝ),
  Dyson.term V lam τ 1 = -lam • ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ, V σ
name: Dyson.term_one
docString: The first weighted Dyson term.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (lam : ℂ) (τ : ℝ),
  Dyson.term V lam τ 0 = 1
name: Dyson.term_zero

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : Fintype α] [Nontrivial α] (σ : Equiv.Perm α),
  σ.IsCycleOn Set.univ ↔ σ.cycleType = {Fintype.card α}
name: Equiv.Perm.isCycleOn_univ_iff_cycleType_eq_singleton_card
docString:
On a nontrivial finite type, a permutation is a single orbit on the whole type
exactly when its cycle type is the singleton containing the ambient cardinality.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (order : Fin s.card ≃ ↥s)
  (orders : π.PartOrders) (h : π.PartOrdersCompatible order orders),
  π.assembleOrder orders (π.shuffleOfOrder order orders h) = order
name: Finpartition.assembleOrder_shuffleOfOrder
docString:
Reassembling a global order from compatible part-local orders and its extracted shuffle is the
original global order.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} (P : Finpartition a)
  (Q : (i : Finset α) → i ∈ P.parts → Finpartition i), P.bind Q ≤ P
name: Finpartition.bind_le
docString: A partition obtained by independently refining every block refines the original partition.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} {σ π : Finpartition a},
  π ≤ σ → (σ.bind fun _B hB => π.restrict ⋯) = π
name: Finpartition.bind_restrict_eq_of_le
docString: Restricting a refinement to every block and binding the results recovers the refinement.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (k : ℕ),
  Fintype.card { σ // (↑σ).parts.card = k } = π.parts.card.stirlingSecond k
name: Finpartition.card_coarsenings_parts_eq_stirlingSecond
docString:
Coarsenings of `π` with exactly `k` blocks are counted by the Stirling number of the second
kind on the block set of `π`.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} (π : Finpartition a) (σ : { σ // π ≤ σ }),
  (π.coarseningsEquivBlockPartitions σ).parts.card = (↑σ).parts.card
name: Finpartition.card_parts_coarseningsEquivBlockPartitions
docString:
Passing from a coarsening of `π` to the induced partition of the block set preserves the
number of blocks.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] (s : Finset α) (k : ℕ),
  Fintype.card { P // P.parts.card = k } = s.card.stirlingSecond k
name: Finpartition.card_parts_eq_stirlingSecond
docString:
Finite partitions with exactly `k` blocks are counted by the Stirling number of the second
kind.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {m : Finset α → ℂ} {A B : Finset α},
  Finpartition.IsIndependentAcross m A B →
    ∀ {T : Finset α}, T ⊆ A ⊔ B → T ≠ ⊥ → Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment m T = Finpartition.splitCumulant m A B T
name: Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment_eq_splitCumulant_of_le
docString: The true cumulant agrees with `splitCumulant` on every nonempty subset of the two regions.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {m : Finset α → ℂ} {A B : Finset α},
  Finpartition.IsIndependentAcross m A B → A ≠ ⊥ → B ≠ ⊥ → Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment m (A ⊔ B) = 0
name: Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment_eq_zero_of_isIndependentAcross
docString: The cumulant of a union of two nonempty independent regions vanishes.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {m : Finset α → ℂ} {A B : Finset α},
  Finpartition.IsIndependentAcross m A B →
    ∀ {T : Finset α}, T ⊆ A ⊔ B → ¬T ⊆ A → ¬T ⊆ B → Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment m T = 0
name: Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment_eq_zero_of_straddles
docString: Any set straddling both independent regions has vanishing cumulant.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommRing R] (κ : Finset α → R) {S : Finset α},
  S ≠ ⊥ → Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment (Finpartition.momentFromCumulant κ) S = κ S
name: Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment_momentFromCumulant
docString: Pointwise Möbius inversion, away from the empty finite set.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} {σ : Finpartition a} {A B B' : Finset α},
  B ∈ σ.parts → B' ∈ σ.parts → A ⊆ B → A ⊆ B' → A ≠ ⊥ → B = B'
name: Finpartition.eq_of_inf_ne_bot
docString: Two blocks containing the same nonempty finite set coincide.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a b : Finset α} {P : Finpartition a} {hb : b ⊆ a} {d : Finset α},
  d ∈ (P.restrict hb).parts ↔ d ≠ ⊥ ∧ ∃ A ∈ P.parts, A ⊓ b = d
name: Finpartition.mem_restrict_iff
docString: Membership in a restricted partition.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommRing R] (m : Finset α → R) {S : Finset α},
  S ≠ ⊥ → Finpartition.momentFromCumulant (Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment m) S = m S
name: Finpartition.momentFromCumulant_cumulantFromMoment
docString: Reverse pointwise inversion, away from the empty finite set.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommSemiring R] (κ : Finset α → R),
  Finpartition.momentFromCumulant κ ∅ = 1
name: Finpartition.momentFromCumulant_empty
docString:
The moment transform is normalized to `1` on the empty set, independently of the input
cumulant value at the empty set.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommSemiring R] (κ : Finset α → R) {s : Finset α}
  {a : α}, a ∈ s → Finpartition.momentFromCumulant κ s = ∑ B, κ ↑B * Finpartition.momentFromCumulant κ (s \ ↑B)
name: Finpartition.momentFromCumulant_eq_sum_blockContaining
docString: The moment sum splits by the block containing a distinguished element.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {S : Finset α},
  S ≠ ∅ → (IncidenceAlgebra.mu ℤ) ⊥ ⊤ = (-1) ^ (S.card - 1) * ↑(S.card - 1).factorial
name: Finpartition.mu_bot_top_eq_factorial
docString:
For a nonempty finite set, the Möbius coefficient from the discrete partition to the
indiscrete partition is `(-1)^(n - 1) (n - 1)!`.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] (S : Finset α),
  (IncidenceAlgebra.mu ℤ) ⊥ ⊤ = if S = ∅ then 1 else (-1) ^ (S.card - 1) * ↑(S.card - 1).factorial
name: Finpartition.mu_bot_top_eq_factorial_ite
docString: Total bottom-to-top formula, including the empty partition lattice.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {S : Finset α} {π σ : Finpartition S},
  π ≤ σ →
    (IncidenceAlgebra.mu ℤ) π σ =
      ∏ B, (-1) ^ ((π.restrict ⋯).parts.card - 1) * ↑((π.restrict ⋯).parts.card - 1).factorial
name: Finpartition.mu_eq_prod_factorial
docString: Explicit product formula for every interval in a finite set-partition lattice.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} {R : Type u_2} [inst_1 : CommRing R] {π σ : Finpartition a},
  π ≤ σ → (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) π σ = ∏ B, (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) (π.restrict ⋯) ⊤
name: Finpartition.mu_eq_prod_restrict
docString: The partition-lattice Möbius function factors over the blocks of the coarser partition.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {S : Finset α} (π : Finpartition S),
  S ≠ ∅ → (IncidenceAlgebra.mu ℤ) π ⊤ = (-1) ^ (π.parts.card - 1) * ↑(π.parts.card - 1).factorial
name: Finpartition.mu_to_top_eq_factorial
docString: The Möbius coefficient from a partition to the top is determined by its number of blocks.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} {R : Type u_2} [inst_1 : CommRing R] (π : Finpartition a),
  (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) π ⊤ = (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) ⊥ ⊤
name: Finpartition.mu_to_top_eq_mu_bot_top_parts
docString: The Möbius function from a partition to the top depends only on its block set.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (orders : π.PartOrders)
  (shuffle : π.PartShuffle), π.PartOrdersCompatible (π.assembleOrder orders shuffle) orders
name: Finpartition.partOrdersCompatible_assembleOrder
docString: The local orders used to assemble a global order are compatible with that assembled order.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (order : Fin s.card ≃ ↥s),
  π.PartOrdersCompatible order (π.partOrdersOfOrder order)
name: Finpartition.partOrdersCompatible_partOrdersOfOrder
docString: The canonical part-local orders are compatible with the ambient order.

name: Finpartition.partitionProduct_bind
docString: Block products factor over a partition constructed by `bind`.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommSemiring R] (κ : Finset α → R) {s : Finset α}
  {a : α} (ha : a ∈ s) (x : (B : Finpartition.BlockContaining s a) × Finpartition (s \ ↑B)),
  Finpartition.partitionProduct κ ((Finpartition.distinguishedBlockEquiv s a ha).symm x) =
    κ ↑x.fst * Finpartition.partitionProduct κ x.snd
name: Finpartition.partitionProduct_distinguishedBlockEquiv_symm

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {m : Finset α → ℂ} {A B : Finset α},
  Finpartition.IsIndependentAcross m A B →
    ∀ (π : Finpartition (A ⊔ B)),
      Finpartition.partitionProduct m π =
        Finpartition.partitionProduct m (π.restrict ⋯) * Finpartition.partitionProduct m (π.restrict ⋯)
name: Finpartition.partitionProduct_eq_mul_of_isIndependentAcross
docString: Partition products factor across independent regions.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {S : Finset α} (π : Finpartition S) {b : Finset α} (hb : b ⊆ S)
  {m : Finset α → ℂ}, m ⊥ = 1 → Finpartition.partitionProduct m (π.restrict hb) = ∏ C ∈ π.parts, m (C ⊓ b)
name: Finpartition.partitionProduct_restrict_eq_prod_inf
docString: A restricted partition product is the product of the corresponding intersections.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommRing R] {S : Finset α},
  S ≠ ∅ → ∀ (f : Finset α → R), Finpartition.partitionProduct f ⊤ = f S
name: Finpartition.partitionProduct_top

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommMonoid M] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s)
  (a : M), a ^ s.card = ∏ B, a ^ (↑B).card
name: Finpartition.pow_card_eq_prod_parts
docString:
A power indexed by `s.card` factors into powers indexed by the cardinalities of the partition
parts.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommSemiring R] (κ : Finset α → R) {S : Finset α},
  S ≠ ∅ → (Finpartition.replicaPolynomial κ S).coeff 1 = κ S
name: Finpartition.replicaPolynomial_coeff_one
docString:
For nonempty support, the coefficient linear in the replica count is exactly the one-block
contribution.

statement:
∀ {F : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing F] {α : Type u_4} [inst_1 : DecidableEq α] (κ : Finset α → F) (S : Finset α),
  Finpartition.replicaPolynomial κ S =
    ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (S.card + 1),
      Polynomial.C (∑ π, ↑(π.parts.card.stirlingSecond k) * Finpartition.partitionProduct κ π) * descPochhammer F k
name: Finpartition.replicaPolynomial_eq_sum_descPochhammer_stirling
docString:
The replica polynomial in the descending-factorial basis, grouped by the number of outer
blocks.  The coefficient of the `k`-th descending factorial is the Stirling-weighted sum over all
fine partitions.

statement:
∀ {F : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing F] {α : Type u_4} [inst_1 : DecidableEq α] (κ : Finset α → F) (S : Finset α),
  Finpartition.replicaPolynomial κ S =
    ∑ π,
      ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (π.parts.card + 1),
        Polynomial.C (↑(π.parts.card.stirlingSecond k) * Finpartition.partitionProduct κ π) * descPochhammer F k
name: Finpartition.replicaPolynomial_eq_sum_stirlingSecond_descPochhammer
docString:
The replica polynomial in the descending-factorial basis.  The Stirling number of the second
kind converts the monomial replica factor for a partition into the falling-factorial basis used by
the fixed-order power-series replica polynomial.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommSemiring R] (κ : Finset α → R) (S : Finset α)
  (n : ℕ), Polynomial.eval (↑n) (Finpartition.replicaPolynomial κ S) = ∑ π, ∑ x, Finpartition.partitionProduct κ π
name: Finpartition.replicaPolynomial_eval_nat_eq_sum_labelings
docString:
Evaluating the replica polynomial at a natural replica number is the sum over independent
replica labelings of the blocks of every partition. Each labeling carries the partition's block
weight.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} (σ : Finpartition a)
  (Q : (B : Finset α) → B ∈ σ.parts → Finpartition B) {B : Finset α} (hB : B ∈ σ.parts), (σ.bind Q).restrict ⋯ = Q B hB
name: Finpartition.restrict_bind_eq
docString: Binding blockwise partitions and restricting to one original block recovers that partition.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} (σ : Finpartition a) {B : Finset α} (hB : B ∈ σ.parts),
  σ.restrict ⋯ = ⊤
name: Finpartition.restrict_self_part_eq_top
docString: A partition restricted to one of its own blocks is the indiscrete partition of that block.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommRing R] (m : Finset α → R) {S : Finset α}
  (π : Finpartition S),
  ∑ ρ ≤ π, (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) ρ π * Finpartition.partitionProduct m ρ =
    Finpartition.partitionProduct (Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment m) π
name: Finpartition.sum_Iic_mu_partitionProduct_eq
docString: Möbius-weighted refinement sums factor into blockwise cumulants.

name: Finpartition.sum_Iic_partitionProduct_eq
docString: Sum of block products over refinements factors into blockwise moments.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] (s : Finset α),
  ∀ a ∈ s, ∀ (f : ℕ → R), ∑ B, f (↑B).card = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range s.card, ↑((s.card - 1).choose k) * f (k + 1)
name: Finpartition.sum_blockContaining_card
docString: Reindex a cardinality-dependent sum over distinguished blocks by their size.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} {R : Type u_2} [inst_1 : CommSemiring R] (π : Finpartition s)
  (globalWeight : Fin s.card ≃ ↥s → R) (localWeight : (B : ↥π.parts) → Fin (↑B).card ≃ ↥↑B → R) (c : R),
  (∀ (orders : π.PartOrders),
      ∑ shuffle, globalWeight (π.assembleOrder orders shuffle) = c * ∏ B, localWeight B (orders B)) →
    ∑ order, globalWeight order = c * ∏ B, ∑ order, localWeight B order
name: Finpartition.sum_order_eq_mul_prod_sum_partOrders
docString:
Summing a weight over all global orders factors through component-local order sums whenever,
for each fixed family of local orders, the shuffle sum is a common scalar times the product of
the corresponding local weights.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommSemiring R] (κ : Finset α → R) (S : Finset α)
  (k : ℕ),
  ∑ σ, Finpartition.partitionProduct (Finpartition.momentFromCumulant κ) ↑σ =
    ∑ ρ, ↑(ρ.parts.card.stirlingSecond k) * Finpartition.partitionProduct κ ρ
name: Finpartition.sum_partitionProduct_momentFromCumulant_partsCard_eq
docString:
Summing products of moments over outer partitions with `k` blocks can be reindexed by the
underlying fine partition.  The multiplicity of a fine partition is the Stirling number counting
its `k`-block coarsenings.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (T : Finset α) (R : α → α → Prop) [inst : DecidableRel R],
  {pq ∈ T.product T | R pq.1 pq.2}.card = ∑ p ∈ T, {q ∈ T | R p q}.card
name: Finset.card_filter_product_eq_sum_card_filter

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : NormedCommRing R] [NormOneClass R] [CompleteSpace R] [inst_3 : Fintype ι]
  (f : ι → ℕ → R) (a : ι → R),
  (∀ (i : ι), HasSum (f i) (a i)) → (∀ (i : ι), Summable fun k => ‖f i k‖) → HasSum (fun n => ∏ i, f i (n i)) (∏ i, a i)
name: Finsupp.hasSum_prod
docString:
**A finite product of absolutely convergent series converges** as a `Finsupp`-indexed
multi-series.

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_3} [inst : NormedField R] [CompleteSpace R] {ι : Type u_4} [inst_2 : Fintype ι] (q : ι → R),
  (∀ (i : ι), ‖q i‖ < 1) → HasSum (fun n => ∏ i, q i ^ n i) (∏ i, (1 - q i)⁻¹)
name: Finsupp.hasSum_prod_geometric
docString: **The geometric-series specialization**.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι] (g : ι → ℕ → ℝ) (b : ι → ℝ),
  (∀ (i : ι), HasSum (g i) (b i)) → (∀ (i : ι) (n : ℕ), 0 ≤ g i n) → HasSum (fun n => ∏ i, g i (n i)) (∏ i, b i)
name: Finsupp.hasSum_prod_nonneg
docString:
**The nonnegative-real finite product of series converges** to the product of the individual
sums, as a `Finsupp`-indexed multi-series.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} [inst : Fintype α] [Finite β] [inst_2 : Fintype γ] (e : α ≃ β × γ)
  (f : β → ℕ) {d : ℕ}, d ∣ Fintype.card γ → d ∣ ∑ x, f (e x).1

docString: A first-coordinate sum is divisible by every divisor of the repeated fiber's cardinality.

name: Fintype.prod_equiv_sigma
docString:
Reindex a commutative product through an equivalence with a dependent sum and split it
into the product over the base and each fiber.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} [inst : Fintype α] [inst_1 : Fintype β] [inst_2 : Fintype γ]

name: Fintype.sum_equiv_fst_eq_card_mul_sum
docString: Reindexing a finite type as `β × γ` counts a first-coordinate summand `card γ` times.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_3} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  [Finite ι] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (coeff : ι → ℂ), Fredholm.diagonalDet coeff = (1 + b.diagonalOp coeff).det
name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_eq_det_one_add_diagonalOp
docString:
On a finite Hilbert basis, the diagonal Fredholm determinant agrees with Mathlib's ordinary
determinant of `1 + diagonalOp b coeff`.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} (coeff : ι → ℂ) (s : Finset ι),
  (∀ i ∉ s, coeff i = 0) → Fredholm.diagonalDet coeff = ∏ i ∈ s, (1 + coeff i)
name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_eq_finsetProd
docString:
If the coefficient family vanishes outside a finite set, the Fredholm determinant reduces to
that finite product.

statement: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} (coeff : ι → ℂ), (Summable fun i => ‖coeff i‖) → (Fredholm.diagonalDet coeff = 0 ↔ ∃ i, coeff i = -1)
name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_eq_zero_iff_exists_coeff_eq_neg_one
docString:
For absolutely summable diagonal data, the determinant vanishes exactly when one coefficient is
`-1`, equivalently when one factor `1 + coeff i` vanishes.

statement: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℂ), Fredholm.diagonalDet coeff = ∏ i, (1 + coeff i)
name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_fintype
docString:
On a finite index type, the diagonal Fredholm determinant is the ordinary finite product of the
diagonal factors.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} (coeff : ι → ℂ),
  (Summable fun i => ‖coeff i‖) → (∀ (i : ι), 1 + coeff i ≠ 0) → Fredholm.diagonalDet coeff ≠ 0
name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_ne_zero
docString: If no diagonal factor vanishes, the absolutely convergent determinant is nonzero.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} (e : κ ≃ ι) (coeff : ι → ℂ),
  Fredholm.diagonalDet (coeff ∘ ⇑e) = Fredholm.diagonalDet coeff
name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_reindex
docString: Equivalent enumerations of the same diagonal coefficients give the same determinant.

statement: ∀ {ι : Type u_1}, (Fredholm.diagonalDet fun x => 0) = 1
name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_zero
docString: The determinant of the zero diagonal perturbation is one.

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] {F G : ℂ → V} {F' G' : V} {A : ℂ},
  HasAlgebraicDerivAt F F' A → HasAlgebraicDerivAt G G' A → HasAlgebraicDerivAt (fun z => F z + G z) (F' + G') A
name: HasAlgebraicDerivAt.add
docString: Algebraic derivatives are additive.

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] {F : ℂ → V} {F' : V} {g : ℂ → ℂ} {g' A : ℂ},

name: HasAlgebraicDerivAt.comp
docString:
Reparametrizing an algebraic-vector-valued family by a scalar differentiable map obeys the
chain rule.

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] {F : ℂ → V} {F' : V} {A : ℂ},
  HasAlgebraicDerivAt F F' A → ∀ (c : ℂ), HasAlgebraicDerivAt (fun z => c • F z) (c • F') A
name: HasAlgebraicDerivAt.const_smul
docString: Multiplying an algebraic-vector-valued family by a constant scalar multiplies its derivative.

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] [inst_2 : AddCommGroup W]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ W] {F : ℂ → V} {F' : V} {A : ℂ},

docString: A complex-linear map transports algebraic derivatives.

name: HasAlgebraicDerivAt.sum
docString: Finite sums preserve algebraic derivatives.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
