name: HilbertBasis.diagonalOpSpectralTraceClass
docString: Bundle a diagonal operator with summable nonnegative real weights as spectral-trace-class.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (a : ι → ℂ), (Summable fun i => ‖a i‖) → ∀ (j : ι), (b.diagonalOp a) (b j) = a j • b j
name: HilbertBasis.diagonalOp_apply_basis
docString: The diagonal operator acts on each basis vector by its corresponding coefficient.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (a : ι → ℂ), (Summable fun i => ‖a i‖) → IsCompactOperator ⇑(b.diagonalOp a)
name: HilbertBasis.diagonalOp_isCompact
docString: A diagonal operator with absolutely summable coefficients is compact.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (a : ι → ℝ),
  (Summable fun i => ‖a i‖) → (∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ a i) → (b.diagonalOp fun i => ↑(a i)).IsPositive
name: HilbertBasis.diagonalOp_isPositive
docString: A diagonal operator with summable real nonnegative coefficients is positive.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (a : ι → ℝ),
  (Summable fun i => ‖a i‖) → (∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ a i) → (b.diagonalOp fun i => ↑(a i)).IsTraceClass
name: HilbertBasis.diagonalOp_isTraceClass
docString: A diagonal operator with absolutely summable nonnegative real coefficients is trace class.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (a : ι → ℂ), (Summable fun i => ‖a i‖) → HasSum (b.diagonalTerm a) (b.diagonalOp a)
name: HilbertBasis.hasSum_diagonalTerm
docString: The defining diagonal rank-one series converges to `diagonalOp`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {ι : Type u_2} (d : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H)
  (x : H), HasSum (fun i => ‖inner ℂ x (d i)‖ ^ 2) (‖x‖ ^ 2)
name: HilbertBasis.hasSum_norm_sq_inner
docString:
**Parseval's identity for a Hilbert basis, in norm-squared form.** For any `x : H`, the
squared-magnitude Fourier coefficients of `x` against a Hilbert basis `d` sum unconditionally to
`‖x‖ ^ 2`.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (coeff : ι → ℂ),
  (Summable fun i => ‖coeff i‖) → ∀ (i : ι), (1 + b.diagonalOp coeff) (b i) = (1 + coeff i) • b i
name: HilbertBasis.one_add_diagonalOp_apply_basis
docString: `1 + diagonalOp b coeff` acts diagonally with factors `1 + coeff i`.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (coeff : ι → ℂ),
  (Summable fun i => ‖coeff i‖) → ∀ (i : ι), coeff i = -1 → ∃ x, x ≠ 0 ∧ (1 + b.diagonalOp coeff) x = 0
name: HilbertBasis.one_add_diagonalOp_has_nonzero_kernel_vector_of_coeff_eq_neg_one
docString:
A coefficient `coeff i = -1` produces a nonzero kernel vector of
`1 + diagonalOp b coeff`.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (coeff : ι → ℂ),
  (Summable fun i => ‖coeff i‖) → Fredholm.diagonalDet coeff = 0 → ∃ x, x ≠ 0 ∧ (1 + b.diagonalOp coeff) x = 0
name: HilbertBasis.one_add_diagonalOp_has_nonzero_kernel_vector_of_diagonalDet_eq_zero
docString:
Vanishing of the absolutely summable diagonal Fredholm determinant produces a nonzero kernel
vector of `1 + diagonalOp b coeff`.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (a : ι → ℝ),
  (Summable fun i => ‖a i‖) → (∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ a i) → (b.diagonalOp fun i => ↑(a i)).spectralTrace = ∑' (i : ι), a i
name: HilbertBasis.spectralTrace_diagonalOp_eq_tsum
docString: The spectral trace of a diagonal operator with nonnegative weights is their sum.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (a : ι → ℂ), (Summable fun i => ‖a i‖) → Summable (b.diagonalTerm a)
name: HilbertBasis.summable_diagonalTerm
docString:
Absolute summability of the coefficients implies summability of the diagonal rank-one
operator series in operator norm.

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} {α : Type u_3} [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : Ring S] [inst_2 : PartialOrder α]
  [inst_3 : LocallyFiniteOrder α] [inst_4 : DecidableEq α] (φ : R →+* S) (x y : α),
  φ ((IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) x y) = (IncidenceAlgebra.mu S) x y
name: IncidenceAlgebra.map_mu_apply
docString: Ring homomorphisms preserve the Möbius function.

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : PartialOrder α] [inst_2 : PartialOrder β]
  [inst_3 : LocallyFiniteOrder α] [inst_4 : LocallyFiniteOrder β] [inst_5 : DecidableEq α] [inst_6 : DecidableEq β]
  (e : α ≃o β) (x y : α), (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) (e x) (e y) = (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) x y
name: IncidenceAlgebra.mu_orderIso_apply
docString: The Möbius function is invariant under an order isomorphism.

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : DecidableEq ι] (β : ι → Type u_3)
  [inst_2 : (i : ι) → PartialOrder (β i)] [inst_3 : (i : ι) → LocallyFiniteOrder (β i)]
  [inst_4 : (i : ι) → DecidableEq (β i)] (t : Finset ι) (x y : (i : ↥t) → β ↑i),
  (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) x y = ∏ i, (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) (x i) (y i)
name: IncidenceAlgebra.mu_pi_finset_apply
docString:
The Möbius function of a finite dependent product is the product of the factor Möbius
functions.

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Fintype α] [inst_2 : PartialOrder α]
  [inst_3 : LocallyFiniteOrder α] [inst_4 : DecidableEq α] {z : α} (x y : { t // z ≤ t }),
  (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) x y = (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) ↑x ↑y
name: IncidenceAlgebra.mu_subtype_ge_apply
docString:
The Möbius function computed in a finite principal upper interval agrees with the ambient
Möbius function.

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Fintype α] [inst_2 : PartialOrder α]
  [inst_3 : LocallyFiniteOrder α] [inst_4 : DecidableEq α] {z : α} (x y : { t // t ≤ z }),
  (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) x y = (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) ↑x ↑y
name: IncidenceAlgebra.mu_subtype_le_apply
docString:
The Möbius function computed in a finite principal lower interval agrees with the ambient
Möbius function.

statement:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3} [inst : RCLike 𝕜] [inst_1 : SeminormedAddCommGroup E]
  [inst_2 : NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [inst_3 : SeminormedAddCommGroup F] [inst_4 : InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F] (x : E) (y : F),
  IsCompactOperator ⇑(((InnerProductSpace.rankOne 𝕜) x) y)
name: InnerProductSpace.isCompactOperator_rankOne
docString: Rank-one continuous linear maps are compact.

statement:
∀ (u v : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  u ⬝ᵥ v =
    u InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x * v InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x +
        u InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y * v InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y +
      u InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z * v InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z
name: InternalSpace.dotProduct_pauliAxis
docString:
The ordinary bilinear dot product on Pauli coefficients is the sum of the three semantic
components. No complex conjugation is introduced.

statement:
∀ (M : InternalSpace.PauliMatrix),
  M =
    InternalSpace.pauliScalarCoefficient M • 1 + InternalSpace.pauliCombination (InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient M)
name: InternalSpace.eq_pauliAffine_coefficients
docString:
Every complex two-level matrix is its scalar Pauli-affine coefficient times the identity plus
the Pauli synthesis of its three axis coefficients.

statement:
∀ (a b : ℂ) (u v : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  (a • 1 + InternalSpace.pauliCombination u) * (b • 1 + InternalSpace.pauliCombination v) =
    (a * b + u ⬝ᵥ v) • 1 + InternalSpace.pauliCombination (a • v + b • u + Complex.I • InternalSpace.pauliCross u v)
name: InternalSpace.pauliAffine_mul_pauliAffine
docString: Product of two scalar-plus-Pauli forms.

statement: ∀ (axis : InternalSpace.PauliAxis), Matrix.IsHermitian (InternalSpace.pauliBasis axis)
name: InternalSpace.pauliBasis_isHermitian
docString: Every matrix in the Pauli basis is Hermitian.

statement: LinearIndependent ℂ InternalSpace.pauliBasis
name: InternalSpace.pauliBasis_linearIndependent
docString: The three Pauli matrices form a linearly independent family over `ℂ`.

statement:
∀ (u v : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  InternalSpace.pauliCombination (u + v) = InternalSpace.pauliCombination u + InternalSpace.pauliCombination v
name: InternalSpace.pauliCombination_add
docString: Pauli synthesis commutes with addition of indexed coefficient families.

statement:
∀ (u : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  InternalSpace.pauliCombination u =
    u InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x • InternalSpace.pauliX + u InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y • InternalSpace.pauliY +
      u InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z • InternalSpace.pauliZ
name: InternalSpace.pauliCombination_eq_components
docString:
Coordinate expansion of the canonical axis-indexed Pauli synthesis. Use this only when a
consumer genuinely needs explicit x/y/z components.

statement:
∀ (u v : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  InternalSpace.pauliCombination u * InternalSpace.pauliCombination v =
    (u ⬝ᵥ v) • 1 + Complex.I • InternalSpace.pauliCombination (InternalSpace.pauliCross u v)
name: InternalSpace.pauliCombination_mul_pauliCombination
docString:
Product of two synthesized Pauli vectors:
`(u·σ)(v·σ) = (u·v) I + i (u×v)·σ`.

statement: ∀ (u : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ), InternalSpace.pauliCombination u * InternalSpace.pauliCombination u = (u ⬝ᵥ u) • 1
name: InternalSpace.pauliCombination_mul_self
docString: The square of a Pauli synthesis is its bilinear coefficient square times the identity.

statement: ∀ (u : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℝ), Matrix.IsHermitian (InternalSpace.pauliCombination fun axis => ↑(u axis))
name: InternalSpace.pauliCombination_ofReal_isHermitian
docString: A Pauli synthesis with real axis coefficients is Hermitian.

statement:
∀ (c : ℂ) (u : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  InternalSpace.pauliCombination (c • u) = c • InternalSpace.pauliCombination u
name: InternalSpace.pauliCombination_smul
docString: Pauli synthesis commutes with scalar multiplication of the indexed coefficient family.

statement: ∀ (M : InternalSpace.PauliMatrix), InternalSpace.pauliScalarCoefficient (-M) = -InternalSpace.pauliScalarCoefficient M
name: InternalSpace.pauliScalarCoefficient_neg

statement:
∀ (M : InternalSpace.PauliMatrix),
  InternalSpace.pauliScalarCoefficient (InternalSpace.pauliZ * M * InternalSpace.pauliZ) =
    InternalSpace.pauliScalarCoefficient M
name: InternalSpace.pauliScalarCoefficient_pauliZ_conjugate
docString: Conjugation by `σ_z` leaves the scalar Pauli coefficient unchanged.

statement:
∀ (a x y z : ℂ),
  a ^ 2 - x ^ 2 - y ^ 2 - z ^ 2 ≠ 0 →
    (a • 1 - (x • InternalSpace.pauliX + y • InternalSpace.pauliY + z • InternalSpace.pauliZ)) *
        (a ^ 2 - x ^ 2 - y ^ 2 - z ^ 2)⁻¹ •
          (a • 1 + (x • InternalSpace.pauliX + y • InternalSpace.pauliY + z • InternalSpace.pauliZ)) =
      1
name: InternalSpace.pauliShiftMatrix_mul_closedInverse
docString:
A coordinate Pauli shift `a I - (x σₓ + y σᵧ + z σ_z)` has the inverse-scaled companion as a
right inverse whenever its quadratic denominator is nonzero.

statement:
∀ (a : ℂ) (u : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  (a • 1 - InternalSpace.pauliCombination u) * (a • 1 + InternalSpace.pauliCombination u) = (a ^ 2 - u ⬝ᵥ u) • 1
name: InternalSpace.pauliShift_mul_companion
docString:
Multiplying opposite-sign Pauli shifts eliminates the Pauli part and leaves the quadratic
bilinear invariant.

statement: ∀ (M : InternalSpace.PauliMatrix), InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient (-M) = -InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient M
name: InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient_neg

statement:
∀ (M : InternalSpace.PauliMatrix),
  InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient (InternalSpace.pauliZ * M * InternalSpace.pauliZ) =
    InternalSpace.pauliZConjugateVector (InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient M)
name: InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient_pauliZ_conjugate
docString: Conjugation by `σ_z` acts on Pauli coefficients by `(uₓ,uᵧ,u_z) ↦ (-uₓ,-uᵧ,u_z)`.

name: InternalSpace.trace_four_eq_pauliCoefficients
docString:
Trace of four arbitrary complex two-level matrices expressed only through their canonical
Pauli scalar/vector coefficients.

statement:
∀ (a b c d : ℂ) (u v w x : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  ((a • 1 + InternalSpace.pauliCombination u) * (b • 1 + InternalSpace.pauliCombination v) *
          (c • 1 + InternalSpace.pauliCombination w) *
        (d • 1 + InternalSpace.pauliCombination x)).trace =
    2 *
      ((a * b + u ⬝ᵥ v) * (c * d + w ⬝ᵥ x) +
        (a • v + b • u + Complex.I • InternalSpace.pauliCross u v) ⬝ᵥ
          (c • x + d • w + Complex.I • InternalSpace.pauliCross w x))
name: InternalSpace.trace_four_pauliAffine
docString:
Trace of four Pauli-affine matrices as one scalar expression. Pairing the first two and last
two factors keeps the result compact and exposes only dot and cross products of Pauli coefficients.

statement:
∀ (a b : ℂ) (u v : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  ((a • 1 + InternalSpace.pauliCombination u) * (b • 1 + InternalSpace.pauliCombination v)).trace = 2 * (a * b + u ⬝ᵥ v)
name: InternalSpace.trace_pauliAffine_mul_pauliAffine
docString: Trace of two Pauli-affine matrices in scalar/vector coefficient form.

statement: ∀ (axis : InternalSpace.PauliAxis), Matrix.trace (InternalSpace.pauliBasis axis) = 0
name: InternalSpace.trace_pauliBasis
docString: Every matrix in the Pauli basis is traceless.

statement:
∀ (axis : InternalSpace.PauliAxis) (u : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  (InternalSpace.pauliBasis axis * InternalSpace.pauliCombination u).trace = 2 * u axis
name: InternalSpace.trace_pauliBasis_mul_pauliCombination
docString: Tracing one Pauli basis matrix against a synthesized Pauli vector selects that coefficient.

statement: ∀ (u : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ), Matrix.trace (InternalSpace.pauliCombination u) = 0
name: InternalSpace.trace_pauliCombination
docString: Every Pauli synthesis is traceless.

statement:
∀ (u : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ) (axis : InternalSpace.PauliAxis),
  (InternalSpace.pauliCombination u * InternalSpace.pauliBasis axis).trace = 2 * u axis
name: InternalSpace.trace_pauliCombination_mul_pauliBasis
docString: Tracing a synthesized Pauli vector against one basis matrix selects that coefficient.

statement:
∀ (u v : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  (InternalSpace.pauliCombination u * InternalSpace.pauliCombination v).trace = 2 * u ⬝ᵥ v
name: InternalSpace.trace_pauliCombination_mul_pauliCombination
docString: The trace pairing of two Pauli syntheses is twice the ordinary bilinear dot product.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α) (f : L2Multiplication.ComplexLInf μ)
  (ψ : L2Multiplication.ComplexL2 μ),
  inner ℂ ψ ((L2Multiplication.multiplicationOperator μ f) ψ) = ∫ (x : α), inner ℂ (↑↑ψ x) (↑↑f x * ↑↑ψ x) ∂μ
name: L2Multiplication.inner_multiplicationOperator_eq_integral
docString:
The `L²` expectation of a bounded multiplication operator is the integral of the pointwise
inner-product density.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α) (f : L2Multiplication.ComplexLInf μ)
  (ψ : L2Multiplication.ComplexL2 μ),
  ((L2Multiplication.multiplicationLinear μ) f) ψ = (L2Multiplication.multiplicationOperator μ f) ψ
name: L2Multiplication.multiplicationLinear_apply

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α) (f : L2Multiplication.ComplexLInf μ)
  (ψ : L2Multiplication.ComplexL2 μ), (L2Multiplication.multiplicationOperator μ f) ψ = f • ψ
name: L2Multiplication.multiplicationOperator_apply

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α) (f : L2Multiplication.ComplexLInf μ),
  ‖L2Multiplication.multiplicationOperator μ f‖ ≤ ‖f‖
name: L2Multiplication.multiplicationOperator_norm_le
docString: The multiplication operator has operator norm at most the `L∞` norm of its multiplier.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α) (f : α → ℝ)
  (hf : MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun x => ↑(f x)) ⊤ μ) (ψ φ : L2Multiplication.ComplexL2 μ),
  inner ℂ ((L2Multiplication.multiplicationOperator μ (L2Multiplication.realMultiplier μ f hf)) ψ) φ =

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3} {G : Type u_4} [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : AddCommGroup E]

∀ {R : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3} {G : Type u_4} [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : AddCommGroup E]

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}

statement:

For a densely defined symmetric partial operator, self-adjointness is equivalent to the reverse
adjoint-domain inclusion. The forward inclusion is already supplied by symmetry.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}

statement:

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}

The range of a nonreal shift of a self-adjoint operator is closed.

If `(A - z) xₙ` converges, the nonreal-shift lower bound makes `xₙ` a Cauchy sequence. Completeness
provides a limit `x`, and the closed graph of the self-adjoint operator recovers `x ∈ D(A)` together
with the limiting value of `A x`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H], IsSelfAdjoint A → ∀ {z : ℂ}, z.im ≠ 0 → (A.shiftDomainMap z).rangeᗮ = ⊥
name: LinearPMap.isSelfAdjoint_shiftDomainMap_range_orthogonal_eq_bot
docString: The orthogonal complement of the range of a nonreal self-adjoint shift is trivial.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}

name: LinearPMap.isSelfAdjoint_shiftDomainMap_surjective
docString: Every nonreal shift of a self-adjoint operator is surjective.

∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}

  [inst_2 : _root_.Module R E] [inst_3 : AddCommGroup F] [inst_4 : _root_.Module R F] [inst_5 : AddCommGroup G]

Membership in the domain of natural-domain composition is exactly the usual operator-product
condition.

∀ {R : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3} {G : Type u_4} [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : AddCommGroup E]

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (y : H),

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

docString: Resolvents commute with applying the generator on its domain in the expected affine form.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

docString: `Commute`-packaged form of pairwise nonreal resolvent commutation.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (y : H), (A.nonrealResolvent hA z hz) y ∈ A.domain
name: LinearPMap.nonrealResolvent_mem_domain
docString: The resolvent value lies in the original unbounded operator domain.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z w : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (hw : w.im ≠ 0),

name: LinearPMap.nonrealResolvent_mul_comm
docString: Bounded nonreal resolvents of one self-adjoint operator commute pairwise.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (x : ↥A.domain),

name: LinearPMap.nonrealResolvent_shift_apply
docString: The bounded resolvent is also a left inverse of the nonreal shift on the original domain.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z w : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (hw : w.im ≠ 0) (y : H),
  (A.nonrealResolvent hA z hz) y - (A.nonrealResolvent hA w hw) y =
    (z - w) • (A.nonrealResolvent hA z hz) ((A.nonrealResolvent hA w hw) y)
name: LinearPMap.nonrealResolvent_sub_nonrealResolvent_apply
docString: Pointwise resolvent identity for the convention `R(z) = (A-z)⁻¹`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (y : H),

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (x : ↥A.domain),

name: LinearPMap.nonrealShiftLinearEquiv_apply

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (B : H →L[ℂ] H), IsSelfAdjoint B → ∀ (t : ℝ) (x : H), ‖(LinearPMap.boundedUnitaryEvolution B t) x - x‖ ≤ ‖B x‖ * |t|
name: LinearPMap.norm_boundedUnitaryEvolution_apply_sub_le
docString:
The displacement under bounded self-adjoint evolution is controlled by the generator on the
initial vector.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (y : H),
  ‖(A.nonrealResolvent hA z hz) y‖ ≤ |z.im|⁻¹ * ‖y‖
name: LinearPMap.norm_nonrealResolvent_le
docString: Pointwise norm estimate for the bounded nonreal resolvent.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (y : H),
  ‖(A.nonrealShiftInverseDomain hA z hz) y‖ ≤ |z.im|⁻¹ * ‖y‖
name: LinearPMap.norm_nonrealShiftInverseDomain_le
docString: The bounded inverse obeys the standard nonreal resolvent estimate pointwise.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (y : H), ‖(A.resolventRegularizer hA r hr) y‖ ≤ ‖y‖
name: LinearPMap.norm_resolventRegularizer_le
docString: The resolvent regularizers are contractions, uniformly in the positive scale `r`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (x : ↥A.domain),
  ‖(A.resolventRegularizer hA r hr) ↑x - ↑x‖ ≤ r⁻¹ * ‖↑A x‖
name: LinearPMap.norm_resolventRegularizer_sub_le
docString: Quantitative domain estimate for the regularizer error.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ) (x : ↥A.domain), ‖(A.stoneEvolution hA t) ↑x - ↑x‖ ≤ ‖↑A x‖ * |t|
name: LinearPMap.norm_stoneEvolution_apply_sub_le_domain
docString:
The limiting Stone evolution inherits the domain displacement estimate
`‖U(t)x - x‖ ≤ ‖A x‖ |t|`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (t s : ℝ),
  A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr (t + s) =
    A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr t * A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr s
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolution_add
docString: Each bounded resolvent approximation gives a one-parameter group.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (t : ℝ) (x : H),
  HasDerivAt (fun τ => (A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr τ) x)
    ((A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr t * -Complex.I • A.boundedSelfAdjointApproximation hA r hr) x) t
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolution_apply_hasDerivAt
docString: The resolvent-approximating evolution satisfies its bounded-generator equation vectorwise.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r), A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr 0 = 1
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolution_zero

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (y : H),
  (A.resolventRegularizer hA r hr) y =
    LinearPMap.regularizerCoefficient✝ r •
      ((A.nonrealResolvent hA (star (LinearPMap.imaginaryParameter✝ r)) ⋯) y -
        (A.nonrealResolvent hA (LinearPMap.imaginaryParameter✝ r) ⋯) y)
name: LinearPMap.resolventRegularizer_apply

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (x : ↥A.domain),
  (A.resolventRegularizer hA r hr) ↑x =
    ↑x -
      ↑(1 / 2) •
        ((A.nonrealResolvent hA (star (↑r * Complex.I)) ⋯) (↑A x) + (A.nonrealResolvent hA (↑r * Complex.I) ⋯) (↑A x))

Pointwise finite-dimensional continuity equation assembled from coordinate-line derivatives.

For each coordinate `i`, `ψSpace i` is the restriction of the wavefunction to the coordinate line
through the selected spatial point, and `ψx i` is its first spatial derivative along that line.

is the coordinate expression

`∂ₜρ + ∑ i, ∂ᵢjᵢ = 0`.

One-dimensional pointwise continuity equation for coordinatewise differentiable time and space
slices of a wavefunction.

The two supplied functions represent the time slice through a fixed spatial point and the spatial
slice at a fixed time. `hsame` identifies their value at the spacetime point under consideration.
No `L²` completion or unbounded-operator assertion is used.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (system : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem H)
  (expectation : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.NormalizedExpectation H) {V : ℝ → H →L[ℂ] H},
  (∀ (s : ℝ), IsSelfAdjoint (V s)) →
    ∀ (A₀ A₁ : H →L[ℂ] H) {β M t : ℝ},
      0 ≤ M →
        (∀ s ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system V s‖ ≤ M) →
          t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
            IntervalIntegrable (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system V)
                MeasureTheory.volume 0 t →
              HasDerivAt
                (fun lam => QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.affinePerturbedExpectation system expectation V A₀ A₁ lam t)
                ((-(Complex.I / ↑system.hbar) •
                    ∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..t,
                      expectation.toContinuousLinearMap
                        ⁅QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A₀ t,
                          QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system V s⁆) +
                  expectation.toContinuousLinearMap (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A₁ t))
                0
name: QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.hasDerivAt_affinePerturbedExpectation_zero_of_bound_kubo
docString:
General bounded Kubo formula for an affine source-dependent measured observable. The response
is the usual commutator integral plus the explicit observable-variation/contact contribution.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (system : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem H)
  (expectation : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.NormalizedExpectation H) (f : ℝ → ℝ) {B : H →L[ℂ] H},
  IsSelfAdjoint B →
    ∀ (A₀ A₁ : H →L[ℂ] H) {β M t : ℝ},
      0 ≤ M →
        (∀ s ∈ Set.Icc 0 β,
            ‖QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f B) s‖ ≤
              M) →
          t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
            IntervalIntegrable
                (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f B))
                MeasureTheory.volume 0 t →
              HasDerivAt
                (fun lam =>
                  QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.affinePerturbedExpectation system expectation
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f B) A₀ A₁ lam t)

                    ∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..t, QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system V s)‖ ≤

    QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.purePointTransitionWeight system data A B mn *

              system.hbar))

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.Parameters),
  params.IsRegular →
    ∀ {energy : ℝ},
      QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.inEnergyDomain params energy →
        QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.discriminant params energy =
          Real.cos (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.barrierWaveNumber params energy * params.barrierWidth) *
              Real.cos (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.wellWaveNumber params energy * params.wellWidth) -
            (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.barrierWaveNumber params energy /
                      QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.wellWaveNumber params energy +
                    QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.wellWaveNumber params energy /
                      QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.barrierWaveNumber params energy) /
                  2 *
                Real.sin (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.barrierWaveNumber params energy * params.barrierWidth) *
              Real.sin (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.wellWaveNumber params energy * params.wellWidth)

dispersion formula rather than an artifact of totalized division.

docString:
Massive-Dirac scalar-disorder first-Born self-energy at an arbitrary signed regulator. This is
the exact finite second moment applied to the corresponding clean propagator, not an exact
disorder-averaged self-energy.

statement:

The canonical exact finite second-moment action becomes scalar multiplication when every
impurity potential is scalar in the Dirac internal space.

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters)
  (greenLoop : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2) (hinvertible : IsUnit (params.shiftMatrix greenLoop)),

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters.inverseShiftMatrix_mul_shiftMatrix
docString: The explicit inverse is also a left inverse of `1 - v_imp G_loop`.

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters)
  (greenLoop : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2) (hinvertible : IsUnit (params.shiftMatrix greenLoop)),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.matrixOperator (params.tMatrix greenLoop hinvertible) =
    ↑params.impurityStrength •
      Ring.inverse (1 - ↑params.impurityStrength • QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.matrixOperator greenLoop)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters.matrixOperator_tMatrix_eq_ringInverse_shift
docString:
On an invertible scalar-impurity shift, the canonical matrix T-matrix becomes the corresponding
totalized operator-ring inverse after applying `matrixOperator`. This connects the family-level
asymptotic route below to the existing `IsUnit`-guarded T-matrix API.

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters)
  (greenLoop : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2) (hinvertible : IsUnit (params.shiftMatrix greenLoop)),
  ‖QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.matrixOperator
        (params.tMatrix greenLoop hinvertible - ↑params.impurityStrength • 1)‖ ≤
    ‖↑params.impurityStrength‖ ^ 2 * ‖QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.matrixOperator greenLoop‖ *
      ‖QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.matrixOperator (params.inverseShiftMatrix greenLoop hinvertible)‖
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters.norm_matrixOperator_tMatrix_sub_bare_le
docString:
In operator norm, the exact T-matrix remainder carries two powers of the impurity strength, up
to the norm of the supplied Green loop and inverse shift.

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters)
  (greenLoop : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2) (hinvertible : IsUnit (params.shiftMatrix greenLoop))
  (inverseBound : ℝ),
  ‖QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.matrixOperator (params.inverseShiftMatrix greenLoop hinvertible)‖ ≤ inverseBound →
    ‖QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.matrixOperator
          (params.tMatrix greenLoop hinvertible - ↑params.impurityStrength • 1)‖ ≤
      ‖↑params.impurityStrength‖ ^ 2 * ‖QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.matrixOperator greenLoop‖ * inverseBound
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters.norm_matrixOperator_tMatrix_sub_bare_le_of_inverse_bound
docString:
With a supplied pointwise bound on the operator norm of the inverse shift, the exact remainder
has an explicit quadratic impurity-strength factor. This does not by itself assert a uniform
small-impurity estimate, Big-O statement, or limit as the impurity strength tends to zero.

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters) (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide)
  (v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax : ℝ),
  broadening ≠ 0 →
    disorderStrength = params.impurityDensity * params.impurityStrength ^ 2 →
      ↑(params.impurityDensity * params.impurityStrength ^ 2) •
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.matrixOperator
            (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGreenLoopMatrix side v m probeEnergy
              broadening 0 hbar pMax) =
        QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornSelfEnergyOfRegulator v m probeEnergy
          (side.regulator broadening) disorderStrength hbar pMax
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters.quadraticCleanLoopSelfEnergy_eq_finiteCutoffContinuumBornSelfEnergyOfRegulator
docString:
Under the explicit convention `W = n_imp v_imp²`, the quadratic clean-loop coefficient of
the scalar-impurity T-matrix self-energy is exactly the existing finite-cutoff continuum Born
self-energy. The linear mean-potential term `n_imp v_imp I` is not included in this identity.

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters)
  (greenLoop : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2) (hinvertible : IsUnit (params.shiftMatrix greenLoop)),
  params.selfEnergy greenLoop hinvertible =
    ↑params.impurityDensity • ↑params.impurityStrength • 1 +
      ↑params.impurityDensity • (params.tMatrix greenLoop hinvertible - ↑params.impurityStrength • 1)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters.selfEnergy_eq_meanPotential_add_tMatrix_remainder
docString:
Exact separation of the scalar mean-potential term from the T-matrix self-energy.
The first term is `n_imp v_imp I`; the second keeps the full T-matrix remainder explicit rather
than identifying the mean term with the zero-mean Born disorder self-energy.

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters)
  (greenLoop : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2) (hinvertible : IsUnit (params.shiftMatrix greenLoop)),
  params.shiftMatrix greenLoop * params.inverseShiftMatrix greenLoop hinvertible = 1
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters.shiftMatrix_mul_inverseShiftMatrix
docString: The explicit inverse is a right inverse of `1 - v_imp G_loop`.

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters)
  (greenLoop : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2) (hinvertible : IsUnit (params.shiftMatrix greenLoop)),
  params.shiftMatrix greenLoop * params.tMatrix greenLoop hinvertible = ↑params.impurityStrength • 1
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters.shiftMatrix_mul_tMatrix
docString: Multiplying the T-matrix by its shift from the left gives the scalar impurity potential.

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters)
  (greenLoop : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2) (hinvertible : IsUnit (params.shiftMatrix greenLoop)),
  params.tMatrix greenLoop hinvertible =
    ↑params.impurityStrength • 1 + ↑params.impurityStrength • (greenLoop * params.tMatrix greenLoop hinvertible)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters.tMatrix_eq_bare_add_loop_tMatrix
docString:
Exact Lippmann--Schwinger fixed-point identity. This follows from invertibility alone and does
not assert convergence of a geometric series.

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters)
  (greenLoop : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2) (hinvertible : IsUnit (params.shiftMatrix greenLoop)),
  params.tMatrix greenLoop hinvertible * params.shiftMatrix greenLoop = ↑params.impurityStrength • 1
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters.tMatrix_mul_shiftMatrix
docString: Multiplying the T-matrix by its shift from the right gives the same scalar impurity potential.

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.ScalarImpurityParameters)

docString:
Exact remainder after subtracting the bare scalar-impurity term. No series
expansion is used.

explicit Fermi radius. At `ε_F = |m|`, this occupied region is empty and `p_F = 0`.

    ((InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℂ)
        ((QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.pointwiseEigenbasisData v m px py hE).eigenbasis band))
      ((QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.pointwiseEigenbasisData v m px py hE).eigenbasis band)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjectorOperator_eq_rankOne_pointwiseEigenbasis
docString:
Away from the Dirac degeneracy, the gauge-independent band projector is the rank-one
projector onto the corresponding vector of the generic pointwise Berry eigenbasis.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (v m px py : ℝ),

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (v m px py : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjector band v m px py =

      (1 +
        InternalSpace.pauliCombination
          (↑(QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bandSign band / QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.energy v m px py) •
            QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.diracPauliCoefficients v m px py))
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjector_eq_pauliCombination
docString:
Pauli/Bloch form of the massive-Dirac band projector. This is the canonical spectral-layer
bridge from the model Hamiltonian to the shared internal-space Pauli algebra.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (v m px py : ℝ),

          py =

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjector_mul_oppositeBand
docString: Away from the band degeneracy, opposite-band projectors are orthogonal in either order.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (v m px py : ℝ),

statement:

    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinBandBlockTrace μ ν target source e v m px py
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinBandBlockTrace_swap
docString: Reversing the current order exchanges the source and target band labels.

statement:
∀ (μ ν : Fin 2) (band : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (e v m px py probeEnergy broadening : ℝ),
  broadening ≠ 0 →
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinBandPairContribution μ ν
        (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.oppositeBand band) band e v m px py probeEnergy broadening =
      -2 * Complex.I *
          ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.lorentzianSpectralKernel
              (probeEnergy - QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bandEnergy band v m px py) broadening) *
        QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.interbandSpectatorCurrentFactor μ ν band e v m px py probeEnergy broadening

docString:
Exact factorization of one direction-indexed interband Bastin pair into its Lorentzian spectral
pole and regular spectator/current factor.

statement:
∀ (e hbar m εF Λ : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinCleanHallConductivityCutoff e hbar m εF Λ =

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinCleanHallConductivityCutoff_eq_intrinsicHallConductivityCutoff
docString:
The canonical clean radial Bastin-pair integral has exactly the same finite-cutoff normalization
as the canonical occupation-derived intrinsic Hall conductivity.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (e v m px py : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.energy v m px py ≠ 0 →
    (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinInterbandBlockDifference 0 1 band e v m px py).im /
        QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.interbandEnergyGap band v m px py ^ 2 =
      -(e ^ 2 * QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.berryCurvature band v m px py)

docString:
The normalized Hall antisymmetric Bastin block is the negative of `e²` times the clean Berry
curvature.

statement:
∀ (μ : Fin 2) (band : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (e v m px py : ℝ),

statement:
∀ (μ ν : Fin 2) (band : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (e v m px py : ℝ),

    -QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinInterbandBlockDifference μ ν band e v m px py
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinInterbandBlockDifference_swap
docString:
Exchanging the two current directions reverses the sign of the interband Bastin block
difference.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (e v m p : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.energy v m p 0 ≠ 0 →
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinBandBlockTrace 0 1 (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.oppositeBand band)
        band e v m p 0 =

scalar entry sum. The negative-radius Green and current blocks are replaced by their exact

statement:
∀ (v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialTraceKernel
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.GaussianCrossedDiagram.psi v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax
      radius =
    have a :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentScalarCoefficient 0 v
        m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have b :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenScalarCoefficient
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have c := b;
    have d :=
      -QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentScalarCoefficient 1 v
          m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have ux :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x 0 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have uy :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y 0 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have uz :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z 0 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have qx :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x 1 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have qy :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y 1 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have qz :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z 1 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have grx :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening
        disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have grz :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening
        disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have amplitude :=
      2 *
        ((a * b - ux * grx + uz * grz) * (c * d + grx * qx - grz * qz) +
              (-a * grx + b * ux + Complex.I * uy * grz) * (c * qx + d * grx - Complex.I * grz * qy) +
            (b * uy - Complex.I * (uz * grx + ux * grz)) * (c * qy + Complex.I * (grz * qx + grx * qz)) +
          (a * grz + b * uz + Complex.I * uy * grx) * (-c * qz + d * grz + Complex.I * grx * qy));
    amplitude + (starRingEnd ℂ) amplitude

insertion retains all of its x/y/z Pauli components and its radial sign is kept explicit.

statement:
∀ (e v m p probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRetardedAdvancedDressedSurfaceAngularTraceRadialCoefficient
      0 0 e v m p probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax =
    have q := ↑(-e) * ↑v;
    have solved :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRetardedAdvancedDressedSourceCurrentCoefficientVector
        0 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    have eR :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveEnergy
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    have massR :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveMass
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    have dR :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonDenominator
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    have eA :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveEnergy
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    have massA :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveMass
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    have dA :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonDenominator
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    ↑(4 * Real.pi) * q ^ 2 *
      (dR⁻¹ * dA⁻¹ * ((eR * eA - massR * massA) * solved 0 - Complex.I * (eA * massR - eR * massA) * solved 1) -
        1 / 2 * (dR⁻¹ ^ 2 * (eR ^ 2 - massR ^ 2) + dA⁻¹ ^ 2 * (eA ^ 2 - massA ^ 2)))

statement:
∀ (e hbar m probeEnergy : ℝ),
  hbar ≠ 0 →
    probeEnergy ≠ 0 →
      have sideJumpType :=
        -(e ^ 2 / QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.planckFromReduced hbar) *
          (2 * m * (probeEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) / (probeEnergy * (probeEnergy ^ 2 + 3 * m ^ 2)));
      have gaussianSkewType :=
        -(e ^ 2 / QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.planckFromReduced hbar) *
          (3 * m * (probeEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) ^ 2 / (2 * probeEnergy * (probeEnergy ^ 2 + 3 * m ^ 2) ^ 2));
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.inPlaneCoefficientVector
          ↑(-e ^ 2 * probeEnergy * m / (Real.pi * hbar * (probeEnergy ^ 2 + 3 * m ^ 2)))
          ↑(-e ^ 2 * probeEnergy * m * (probeEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) /
              (Real.pi * hbar * (probeEnergy ^ 2 + 3 * m ^ 2) ^ 2)) =
        QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.inPlaneCoefficientVector
          ↑(QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.intrinsicHallConductivity e hbar m probeEnergy + 3 / 4 * sideJumpType)
          ↑(1 / 4 * sideJumpType + gaussianSkewType)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.orderedXYRungSolvedProvenanceConductivityLimit_eq_intrinsic_sideJumpType_gaussianSkewType_partition
docString:
The physically normalized concrete provenance vector partitions the Ado Eq. (12) mechanisms
from I. A. Ado et al., *EPL* **111**, 37004 (2015),
[doi:10.1209/0295-5075/111/37004](https://doi.org/10.1209/0295-5075/111/37004).
The paper's Eqs. (12a-c) are the intrinsic, side-jump, and non-crossing-skew components; the
theorem below only formalizes the ordered finite-cutoff provenance partition.
The side-jump-type term is shared between the two provenance components rather than attached to only
one of them. The `sideJumpType` and `gaussianSkewType` names are local to this theorem statement and
do not create primitive mechanism APIs.

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.scalarImpurityTMatrixOperator_sub_bare_isBigO_sq
docString:
For a fixed Green loop, the operator-valued scalar-impurity T-matrix has a genuine quadratic
remainder at zero impurity strength:
`T(v_imp) - v_imp I = O(v_imp²)`.
The use of `Ring.inverse` only totalizes the family away from the unit neighborhood; locally it is
the ordinary inverse by `eventually_isUnit_scalarImpurityShiftMatrix`.

statement:
∀ (e hbar v m fermiEnergy disorderStrength : ℝ) (hvelocity : v ≠ 0) (hhbar : 0 < hbar)
  (hdisorder : 0 < disorderStrength) (hmF : |m| < fermiEnergy),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureRelaxationTimeLongitudinalConductivity e hbar v m fermiEnergy
      (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornUpperBandPositiveTransportLifetime v m fermiEnergy
        disorderStrength hbar hvelocity hhbar hdisorder hmF) =
    e ^ 2 * hbar * v ^ 2 * (fermiEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) / (Real.pi * disorderStrength * (fermiEnergy ^ 2 + 3 * m ^ 2))
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureRelaxationTimeLongitudinalConductivity_bornTransportLifetime_eq
docString:
The zero-temperature massive-Dirac RTA benchmark evaluated on the microscopic Born transport
lifetime has the explicit `1/W` form

`σxx = e² ℏ v² (εF² - m²) / [π W (εF² + 3 m²)]`.

The positivity assumptions are exactly those used to package the microscopic lifetime as a
`PositiveTransportLifetime`; no finite clean-disorder limit is asserted.

statement:

    v ≠ 0 →
      |m| < fermiEnergy →
        QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureRelaxationTimeLongitudinalConductivity e hbar v m fermiEnergy
            transportLifetime =
          e ^ 2 * transportLifetime.lifetime * (fermiEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) / (4 * Real.pi * hbar ^ 2 * fermiEnergy)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureRelaxationTimeLongitudinalConductivity_eq
docString:
Closed single-cone zero-temperature massive-Dirac relaxation-time benchmark

`σxx^RTA = e² τ_tr (ε_F² - m²) / (4π ℏ² ε_F)`.

is positive in the strict metallic regime.

    ↑p *
      (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel z * coefficients.constant +

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] {ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble}
  {energy broadening : ℝ} (solution : ensemble.FiniteSCBASolution energy broadening) (charge : H →L[ℂ] H),
  ensemble.ChargeSymmetry charge →
    ∀
      (hinvertible :
        IsUnit
          (1 -
            ensemble.retardedAdvancedLadderCLM (solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded)
              (solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced))),
      (QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameter QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced energy broadening -
            QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameter QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded energy broadening) •
          (solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded *
              QuantumTheory.Transport.resummedLadderVertex
                (ensemble.retardedAdvancedLadderCLM (solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded)
                  (solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced))
                hinvertible charge *
            solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced) =
        solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded * charge -
          charge * solution.green QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.FiniteSCBASolution.resummedLadderVertex_charge_ward_consistency
docString:
Finite SCBA/RA charge-vertex Ward consistency. Under the minimal charge-symmetry interface and
the same conditional ladder invertibility used by the generic resummation, the generic corrected
charge vertex `Γ_Q = (I - L_RA)⁻¹ Q` obeys

`(zᴬ - zᴿ) • (Ḡᴿ Γ_Q Ḡᴬ) = Ḡᴿ Q - Q Ḡᴬ`.

For `Q = 1`, the right-hand side is `Ḡᴿ - Ḡᴬ`.

  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (energy regulator : ℝ), regulator ≠ 0 → IsUnit (ensemble.averagedGreenOfRegulator energy regulator)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.averagedGreenOfRegulator_isUnit
docString:
At any nonzero signed regulator the exact averaged Green operator is a unit in arbitrary
Hilbert-space dimension.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (energy regulator : ℝ),
  regulator ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (ω : Ω),
      ensemble.configurationGreenOfRegulator energy regulator ω =
        ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator +
          ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator * ↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω) *
            ensemble.configurationGreenOfRegulator energy regulator ω
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.configurationGreenOfRegulator_eq_free_add_dyson_left
docString:
Exact left-oriented configuration Dyson identity at an arbitrary nonzero signed regulator,
`Gω = G₀ + G₀ Vω Gω`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (energy regulator : ℝ),
  regulator ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (ω : Ω),
      ensemble.configurationGreenOfRegulator energy regulator ω =
        ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator +
          ensemble.configurationGreenOfRegulator energy regulator ω * ↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω) *
            ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.configurationGreenOfRegulator_eq_free_add_dyson_right
docString:
Exact right-oriented configuration Dyson identity at an arbitrary nonzero signed regulator,
`Gω = G₀ + Gω Vω G₀`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (energy regulator : ℝ),
  regulator ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (ω : Ω),
      ensemble.configurationGreenOfRegulator energy regulator ω =
        ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator +
            ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator * ↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω) *
              ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator +
          ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator * ↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω) *
                ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator *
              ↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω) *
            ensemble.configurationGreenOfRegulator energy regulator ω
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.configurationGreenOfRegulator_eq_secondOrder_add_exactRemainder_left
docString: Exact left-oriented second-order Dyson expansion at an arbitrary nonzero signed regulator.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (energy regulator : ℝ),
  regulator ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (ω : Ω),

          ensemble.configurationGreenOfRegulator energy regulator ω * ↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω) *
                ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator *
              ↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω) *
            ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.configurationGreenOfRegulator_eq_secondOrder_add_exactRemainder_right
docString: Exact right-oriented second-order Dyson expansion at an arbitrary nonzero signed regulator.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (energy regulator : ℝ),
  regulator ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (ω : Ω),
      QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy (ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator)
        (ensemble.configurationGreenOfRegulator energy regulator ω) ↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.configurationGreenOfRegulator_isSelfEnergy
docString:
The exact Green operator of each disorder configuration satisfies the canonical two-sided
Dyson self-energy relation, with the configuration potential as the self-energy insertion.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (kernel : H →L[ℂ] H),
  ensemble.exactSecondMoment kernel =
    ensemble.operatorAverage fun ω => ↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω) * kernel * ↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.exactSecondMoment_eq_operatorAverage
docString: The canonical exact second moment is the normalized finite operator average `E[Vω X Vω]`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (amplitude : Ω → ℝ),
  (∀ (ω : Ω), ↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω) = ↑(amplitude ω) • 1) →
    ∀ (kernel : H →L[ℂ] H), ensemble.exactSecondMoment kernel = ensemble.scalarSecondMomentStrength amplitude • kernel
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.exactSecondMoment_eq_scalarSecondMomentStrength_smul
docString:
If every impurity potential is scalar, `Vω = uω I`, the exact second-moment action is scalar
multiplication by `E[uω²]`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (kernel right : H →L[ℂ] H),
  (∀ (ω : Ω), Commute (↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω)) right) →
    ensemble.exactSecondMoment kernel * right = ensemble.exactSecondMoment (kernel * right)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.exactSecondMoment_mul_of_commutes
docString:
Right equivariance of the exact second moment. If every impurity potential commutes with a
bounded operator, that operator can be moved through the right side of the second-moment action.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (kernel : H →L[ℂ] H), ensemble.exactSecondMoment (star kernel) = star (ensemble.exactSecondMoment kernel)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.exactSecondMoment_star
docString:
The exact second-moment action preserves adjoints because every impurity potential is
self-adjoint and every ensemble weight is real.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (left right : H →L[ℂ] H),
  ensemble.exactSecondMoment (left - right) = ensemble.exactSecondMoment left - ensemble.exactSecondMoment right
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.exactSecondMoment_sub
docString:
The exact second-moment action preserves subtraction because its canonical realization is
complex-linear.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (energy regulator : ℝ) (hregulator : regulator ≠ 0),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy (ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator)
    (ensemble.averagedGreenOfRegulator energy regulator)
    (ensemble.exactSelfEnergyOfRegulator energy regulator hregulator)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.exactSelfEnergyOfRegulator_isSelfEnergy
docString:
The canonical exact finite-disorder self-energy satisfies the exact two-sided Dyson relation at
any nonzero signed regulator.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (energy regulator : ℝ) (hregulator : regulator ≠ 0) (selfEnergy : H →L[ℂ] H),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy (ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator)
      (ensemble.averagedGreenOfRegulator energy regulator) selfEnergy ↔
    selfEnergy = ensemble.exactSelfEnergyOfRegulator energy regulator hregulator
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.isSelfEnergy_iff_eq_exactSelfEnergyOfRegulator
docString:
At a nonzero signed regulator, the canonical exact self-energy is the unique self-energy
satisfying the exact two-sided Dyson relation for the clean and disorder-averaged Green operators.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (left kernel : H →L[ℂ] H),
  (∀ (ω : Ω), Commute (↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω)) left) →
    left * ensemble.exactSecondMoment kernel = ensemble.exactSecondMoment (left * kernel)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.mul_exactSecondMoment_of_commutes
docString:
Left equivariance of the exact second moment. If every impurity potential commutes with a
bounded operator, that operator can be moved through the left side of the second-moment action.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (operator : Ω → H →L[ℂ] H),
  (ensemble.operatorAverage fun ω => star (operator ω)) = star (ensemble.operatorAverage operator)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.operatorAverage_star
docString: Exact finite operator averaging commutes with adjunction because every ensemble weight is real.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (self : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble) (ω : Ω),
  0 ≤ self.probability ω
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.probability_nonneg

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (self : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble),
  ∑ ω, self.probability ω = 1
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.probability_sum

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (retardedGreen advancedGreen vertex : H →L[ℂ] H),
  (ensemble.retardedAdvancedLadderCLM retardedGreen advancedGreen) vertex =
    ensemble.exactSecondMoment (retardedGreen * vertex * advancedGreen)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.retardedAdvancedLadderCLM_apply
docString:
Evaluation of the finite covariance ladder is the expected operator insertion
`C₂(Gᴿ Γ Gᴬ)`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (energy regulator : ℝ),
  star (ensemble.averagedGreenOfRegulator energy regulator) = ensemble.averagedGreenOfRegulator energy (-regulator)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.star_averagedGreenOfRegulator
docString: Adjointing the exact finite disorder-averaged Green operator reverses the signed regulator.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (energy regulator : ℝ),
  star (ensemble.bornSelfEnergyOfRegulator energy regulator) = ensemble.bornSelfEnergyOfRegulator energy (-regulator)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.star_bornSelfEnergyOfRegulator
docString: Adjointing the first-Born self-energy reverses the signed regulator.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : Ring A] {freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy freeInverse dressedInverse : A},
  freeInverse * freeGreen = 1 →
    freeGreen * freeInverse = 1 →
      dressedInverse * dressedGreen = 1 →
        dressedGreen * dressedInverse = 1 →
          (QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy ↔
            selfEnergy = freeInverse - dressedInverse)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy.iff_eq_inverse_sub_inverse
docString:
For two-sided inverses, the two-sided Dyson relation is equivalent to the inverse-difference
definition of self-energy.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : Ring A] {freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy : A},
  QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy →
    dressedGreen = freeGreen + freeGreen * selfEnergy * dressedGreen
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy.leftDyson
docString: The left-oriented Dyson equation carried by an abstract self-energy relation.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : Ring A] {freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy freeShift dressedShift : A},
  freeGreen * freeShift = 1 →
    freeShift * freeGreen = 1 →
      dressedShift * dressedGreen = 1 →
        dressedGreen * dressedShift = 1 →
          freeShift = dressedShift + selfEnergy → QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy.of_shift
docString:
A Dyson self-energy follows from two-sided inverse equations for the free and dressed shifts
together with `freeShift = dressedShift + selfEnergy`.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : Ring A] {freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy : A},
  QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy →
    dressedGreen = freeGreen + dressedGreen * selfEnergy * freeGreen
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy.rightDyson
docString: The right-oriented Dyson equation carried by an abstract self-energy relation.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : Ring A] [inst_1 : StarRing A] {freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy : A},
  QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy →
    QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy (star freeGreen) (star dressedGreen) (star selfEnergy)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy.star_closed
docString:
The two-sided Dyson self-energy relation is preserved by adjunction. The two Dyson orientations
are exchanged because `star` reverses noncommutative multiplication order.

name: QuantumTheory.Transport.PurePointOccupationInterpolation.occupation_matches_probability

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} (system : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem H)
  {data : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.PurePointLehmannData system ι}
  (interpolation : QuantumTheory.Transport.PurePointOccupationInterpolation system data) (m n : ι),
  ↑(data.probability m) - ↑(data.probability n) =
    ∫ (energy : ℝ) in data.energy n..data.energy m, interpolation.occupationDerivative energy
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.PurePointOccupationInterpolation.probability_sub_eq_integral
docString:
The occupation difference of two energy eigenstates is the oriented integral of the
occupation derivative between their energies.

statement:

statement:
∀ (self : QuantumTheory.Transport.RegularizedStredaIntegralData),

statement:
∀ {K : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup K] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ K] [inst_2 : NormedAddCommGroup H]
  [inst_3 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_4 : CompleteSpace H] {Lstar : Submodule ℤ K} [inst_5 : FiniteDimensional ℂ H]

docString: The Fermi level lies in the resolvent set at every momentum.

statement:
∀ {K : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup K] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ K] [inst_2 : NormedAddCommGroup H]
  [inst_3 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_4 : CompleteSpace H] {Lstar : Submodule ℤ K} [inst_5 : FiniteDimensional ℂ H]
  (self : QuantumTheory.Transport.Topology.GappedBlochSystem Lstar) (k : K) (energy : ℝ) (x : H),

docString: Spectral characterization of the occupied projector on Hamiltonian eigenvectors.

statement:

The proof uses self-adjointness of the projector and its directional derivatives, the resulting
skew-adjointness of their commutator, cyclicity of the finite-dimensional trace, and
`Tr(A⋆) = star (Tr A)`.

      (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarPoint2D radius angle) =
    ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
      ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
        ↑p *
          (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) * (coefficients p).constant +
              QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierFirstCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
                (↑(Real.cos angle) * (coefficients p).firstCosine + ↑(Real.sin angle) * (coefficients p).firstSine) +
            QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierSecondCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
              ((↑(Real.cos angle) ^ 2 - ↑(Real.sin angle) ^ 2) * (coefficients p).secondCosine +
                ↑(Real.cos angle) * ↑(Real.sin angle) * (coefficients p).secondMixed))

docString:

statement:

      omega eta mn

statement:

docString:
At positive switching rate, one pure-point Lehmann transition equals its retarded-resolvent
Kubo–Bastin form.

statement:

statement:

carried entirely by the residual Fermi-sea term.

statement:

docString:
Integration by parts gives the regularized surface/sea decomposition on the finite energy
interval. Every derivative, integrability, and boundary hypothesis is stored in `data`.

statement:
∀ {KSpace : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup KSpace] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ KSpace]
  (hamiltonian current₁ current₂ : KSpace →L[ℂ] KSpace) (energy broadening : ℝ),

docString:
Pointwise finite-broadening decomposition into the surface-primitive derivative and the
residual sea kernel.

statement:

Simultaneously reversing both current vertices leaves the canonical Bastin operator
integrand unchanged.

statement:

docString: Finite pure-point spectral expansion of the canonical ordinary-trace Bastin integrand.

statement:

name: QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedBastinTraceIntegrand_eq_surfaceDerivative_add_residualSea
docString: The pointwise operator decomposition descends to the ordinary finite-dimensional trace.

statement:
∀ (data : QuantumTheory.Transport.RegularizedStredaIntegralData),

docString:
If the occupation derivative vanishes identically, the regularized Fermi-surface contribution
vanishes. This is a smooth finite-interval statement, not a zero-temperature distributional claim.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : FiniteDimensional ℂ H]
  (hamiltonian current₁ current₂ : H →L[ℂ] H) (energy broadening : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedStredaResidualSeaTraceKernel hamiltonian current₁ current₂ energy broadening =
    -QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedStredaResidualSeaTraceKernel hamiltonian current₂ current₁ energy broadening
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedStredaResidualSeaTraceKernel_swap
docString:
The finite-broadening residual sea trace is antisymmetric under exchange of the two current
vertices. This is an exact finite-dimensional trace-cyclicity identity.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : FiniteDimensional ℂ H]
  (hamiltonian measuredVertex sourceVertex : H →L[ℂ] H) (energy broadening : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedStredaSurfacePrimitiveTrace hamiltonian measuredVertex sourceVertex energy
      broadening =
    QuantumTheory.Transport.suppliedGreenStredaSurfacePrimitiveTraceKernel measuredVertex
      (QuantumTheory.Transport.retardedResolvent hamiltonian energy broadening) sourceVertex
      (QuantumTheory.Transport.advancedResolvent hamiltonian energy broadening)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedStredaSurfacePrimitiveTrace_eq_suppliedGreen
docString:
For arbitrary current vertices, the clean regularized Středa surface primitive is exactly the
supplied-Green `RA - RR/AA` trace kernel evaluated on the canonical resolvents.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype ι] [inst_4 : FiniteDimensional ℂ H]
  (system : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem H)
  (data : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.PurePointLehmannData system ι) (current₁ current₂ : H →L[ℂ] H)
  (broadening lowerEnergy upperEnergy : ℝ) (occupation : ℝ → ℂ),
  0 < broadening →
    QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedTracedBastinEnergyIntegral (↑system.hamiltonian) current₁ current₂ broadening
        lowerEnergy upperEnergy occupation =
      QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedBastinSpectralEnergyIntegral system data current₁ current₂ broadening
        lowerEnergy upperEnergy occupation
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedTracedBastinEnergyIntegral_eq_spectral
docString:
At positive broadening, the canonical traced Bastin energy integral is exactly its finite
pure-point spectral energy integral.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (hamiltonian candidate : H →L[ℂ] H),
  IsSelfAdjoint hamiltonian →
    ∀ (energy regulator : ℝ),
      regulator ≠ 0 →
        ((algebraMap ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H)) (QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameterOfRegulator energy regulator) -
                hamiltonian) *
              candidate =
            1 →
          resolvent hamiltonian (QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameterOfRegulator energy regulator) = candidate
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.resolvent_eq_of_spectralShift_mul_eq_one
docString:
A candidate right inverse of the spectral shift at an arbitrary nonzero signed regulator equals
the canonical resolvent.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (hamiltonian : H →L[ℂ] H),
  IsSelfAdjoint hamiltonian →
    ∀ {v : H} {eigenvalue : ℝ},
      hamiltonian v = ↑eigenvalue • v →
        ∀ (energy regulator : ℝ),
          regulator ≠ 0 →
            (resolvent hamiltonian (QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameterOfRegulator energy regulator)) v =
              (QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameterOfRegulator energy regulator - ↑eigenvalue)⁻¹ • v
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.resolvent_spectralParameterOfRegulator_apply_eigenvector
docString:
A resolvent with arbitrary nonzero signed regulator acts on a Hamiltonian eigenvector by the
corresponding scalar resolvent factor.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] (system : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem H)
  (data : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.PurePointLehmannData system ι) (energy regulator : ℝ),
  regulator ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (n : ι),
      (resolvent (↑system.hamiltonian) (QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameterOfRegulator energy regulator))
          (data.basis n) =
        (QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameterOfRegulator energy regulator - ↑(data.energy n))⁻¹ • data.basis n
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.resolvent_spectralParameterOfRegulator_apply_purePointBasis_at_energy
docString:
A resolvent with arbitrary nonzero signed regulator acts diagonally on the supplied pure-point
energy basis.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (hamiltonian : H →L[ℂ] H),
  IsSelfAdjoint hamiltonian →
    ∀ (energy regulator : ℝ),
      regulator ≠ 0 →
        resolvent hamiltonian (QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameterOfRegulator energy regulator) *
            ((algebraMap ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H)) (QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameterOfRegulator energy regulator) -
              hamiltonian) =
          1
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.resolvent_spectralParameterOfRegulator_mul_spectralShift
docString:
For an arbitrary nonzero signed regulator, its resolvent multiplied by the spectral shift is
the identity.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]

name: QuantumTheory.Transport.resolvent_spectralParameterOfRegulator_sq_apply_purePointBasis_at_energy
docString:
On a pure-point energy basis, the square of a resolvent with arbitrary nonzero signed regulator
has the squared scalar denominator.

statement:

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

statement:

statement:

For an arbitrary nonzero signed regulator, the spectral shift multiplied by its resolvent is

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

The side-indexed shifted operator multiplied by the canonical spectral resolvent is the

statement:

statement:

statement:
