name: QuantumTheory.Transport.star_spectralParameterOfRegulator

statement:
∀ (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide) (gap offset broadening : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.targetCenteredSourceCoefficient side gap offset broadening =

name: QuantumTheory.Transport.targetCenteredSourceCoefficient_eq
docString: Target-centered source denominator in the explicit `gap + offset + iγ` form.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {l : Filter ι} {f g width : ι → ℝ} {a b : ℝ},
  Filter.Tendsto f l (nhds a) →
    0 < a →
      Filter.Tendsto g l (nhds b) →
        b < 0 →
          Filter.Tendsto width l (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) →
            Filter.Tendsto (fun x => Real.arctan (f x / width x) - Real.arctan (g x / width x)) l (nhds Real.pi)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.tendsto_arctan_div_sub_arctan_div_nhdsGT_zero
docString:
If two continuously moving endpoints approach opposite sides of a resonance while a common
positive width tends to zero, their arctangent phase difference tends to `π`.

statement:
∀ (distance : ℝ),
  0 < distance →
    Filter.Tendsto (fun broadening => Real.arctan (distance / broadening)) (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0))
      (nhds (Real.pi / 2))
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.tendsto_arctan_pos_div_broadening
docString:
For every fixed positive distance, `arctan(distance / η)` tends to `π / 2` as positive
broadening tends to zero.

statement:
∀ (radius : ℝ),
  0 < radius →
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun broadening =>

∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

  (β : ℝ),
  β ≠ 0 →
    QuantumTheory.energyExpValue ρ Hop - 1 / β * (QuantumTheory.vonNeumannEntropy ρ).toReal =
        -(1 / β) * Real.log (QuantumTheory.gibbsOp Hop β).spectralTrace →
      ∑' (a : ρ.op.EigenvectorIndex),
            (QuantumTheory.gibbsOp Hop β).diagonalExpectationValue ⋯ (ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily ⋯ a) =
          (QuantumTheory.gibbsOp Hop β).spectralTrace ∧
        (∀ (a : ρ.op.EigenvectorIndex),
            ↑a.fst =
              (QuantumTheory.gibbsOp Hop β).diagonalExpectationValue ⋯ (ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily ⋯ a) /
                (QuantumTheory.gibbsOp Hop β).spectralTrace) ∧
          ∀ (a : ρ.op.EigenvectorIndex),
            Real.exp (-β * (↑Hop).diagonalExpectationValue ⋯ (ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily ⋯ a)) =
              (QuantumTheory.gibbsOp Hop β).diagonalExpectationValue ⋯ (ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily ⋯ a)

eigenvalue equals the normalized Gibbs diagonal weight, and every Peierls–Bogoliubov bound is
saturated.

summability needed to make the entropy operator trace-class.

statement:
∀ {Label : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring A] [inst_1 : Algebra ℂ A] (element : Label → A)
  (exchangeCoeff : Label → Label → ℂ) (ζ : ℂ),
  (∀ (C D : Label), element C * element D = exchangeCoeff C D • 1 + ζ • (element D * element C)) →
    ∀ (C : Label) (l : List Label),
      element C * (List.map element l).prod =
        ScalarExchange.peelSum element exchangeCoeff ζ C l + ζ ^ l.length • ((List.map element l).prod * element C)

ordered product.

statement:

  (∀ p ∈ l, C * p.1 = p.2 • 1 + ζ • (p.1 * C)) →
    C * (List.map Prod.fst l).prod =
      ScalarExchange.peelSumWithCoefficients ζ l + ζ ^ l.length • ((List.map Prod.fst l).prod * C)

docString:
Repeatedly apply a scalar exchange relation between one fixed element and the factors of a
coefficient-paired list. This form is useful when the exchange coefficients depend on the fixed
element, so no relations between the factors themselves are required.

docString: Position-indexed expansion when each factor carries its exchange coefficient.

the diagram. The proof reindexes global vertex orders into component-local orders and shuffles, then
uses the finite-family ordered-simplex shuffle identity for the time integrals.

      (d : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode) N S)
      (order : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexOrder S),

name: SecondQuantization.Bosonic.QuarticDiagram.freeGibbsExpectation_eq_orderedThermalWickSum

The concrete Gibbs expectation of the ordered quartic local-leg product is exactly the sum over
the pairing amplitudes carried by the existing quartic diagram combinatorics.

statement:

  (d : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode) N S)
  (orders : d.ComponentVertexOrders) (shuffle : d.ComponentShuffle) (B : ↥d.vertexGraph.componentPartitionOn.parts)
  (a b : Fin (2 * (2 * (↑B).card))),
  SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeThermalPairValue ε β
      (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.QuarticDiagram.orderedFreeThermalFieldFamily d (d.assembleVertexOrder orders shuffle)
        (d.componentOrderedLeg shuffle B a))
      (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.QuarticDiagram.orderedFreeThermalFieldFamily d (d.assembleVertexOrder orders shuffle)
        (d.componentOrderedLeg shuffle B b)) =
    SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeThermalPairValue ε β
      (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.QuarticDiagram.orderedFreeThermalFieldFamily (d.restrictComponent ⋯) (orders B) a)
      (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.QuarticDiagram.orderedFreeThermalFieldFamily (d.restrictComponent ⋯) (orders B) b)
name: SecondQuantization.Bosonic.QuarticDiagram.freeThermalPairValue_componentOrderedLeg
docString:
The free thermal pair kernel agrees between a component-local ordered pair and its image in an
assembled global order.

  SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeEigenvalue ε)
      (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.quarticInteractionOn support g) n t =
    ∑ q,
      SecondQuantization.Common.quarticDysonSequenceCoeff ε g (fun i => ↑(q i)) t •
        SecondQuantization.Common.quarticVertexSequenceOperator SecondQuantization.Bosonic.create
          SecondQuantization.Bosonic.annihilate fun i => ↑(q i)

docString:
The actual arbitrary-occupation-space Dyson coefficient of a finitely supported bosonic quartic
interaction is a finite sum over support-valued vertex-label sequences. Each summand is a static
bare operator product multiplied by its scalar ordered-simplex Dyson coefficient.

The ambient mode type need not be finite, and no infinite Gibbs sum/integral interchange is used.

docString:
Every finite Dyson coefficient of a finitely supported quartic interaction belongs to the
free-Gibbs domain. This is proved coefficientwise from the finite vertex-sequence expansion and does

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [Finite Mode] (support : Finset (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode)) (ε : Mode → ℝ)
  (β : ℝ),
  (∀ (i : Mode), 0 < β * ε i) →
    ∀ (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ),
      SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsDysonCoeff ε β (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.quarticInteractionOn support g) n
          t =
        ∑ q,
          SecondQuantization.Common.quarticDysonSequenceCoeff ε g (fun i => ↑(q i)) t *
            ∑ pairing,
              pairing.evaluation (Combinatorics.Pairing.weight SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.boson pairing)
                fun a b =>
                SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeThermalPairValue ε β
                  (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.quarticFreeThermalFieldFamily (fun i => ↑(q i)) a)
                  (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.quarticFreeThermalFieldFamily (fun i => ↑(q i)) b)
name: SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsDysonCoeff_quarticInteractionOn_eq_sum_pairingEvaluation
docString:
The convergence-aware Gibbs expectation of a finite-order quartic Dyson coefficient is a finite
sum over support-valued vertex sequences and bosonic pairings. The scalar
`quarticDysonSequenceCoeff` carries the full ordered-simplex imaginary-time integration, while the
pairing evaluation is the existing static free-boson thermal Wick factor.

statement:

  (∀ (i : Mode), 0 < β * ε i) →
    ∀ (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) {N : ℕ} (S : Finset (Fin N))
      (order : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexOrder S) (t : ℝ),
      SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsDysonCoeff ε β (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.quarticInteraction g) S.card t =
        ∑ d, SecondQuantization.Bosonic.QuarticDiagram.orderedDysonThermalAmplitude ε β g d order t
name: SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsDysonCoeff_quarticInteraction_eq_sum_orderedDysonThermalAmplitude
docString:
The physical finite-order bosonic quartic Dyson coefficient is the sum of fixed-order physical
quartic diagram amplitudes. This is the canonical reindexing of the concrete
`vertex sequence × pairing` expansion through `Common.quarticDiagramEquivOrderedData`.

docString: The normalized free Gibbs expectation is additive on its explicit summability domain.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [Fintype Mode] [inst : DecidableEq Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ),
  (∀ (k : Mode), 0 < β * ε k) →
    ∀ (i j : Mode),
      SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsSummable ε β
          (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Bosonic.create j) →
        SecondQuantization.Bosonic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Bosonic.create j ∈
            SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsDomain ε β ∧
          (1 - Complex.exp ↑(-ε i * β)) *
              SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsExpectation ε β
                (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Bosonic.create j) =
            if i = j then 1 else 0

analytic-domain witness for the composite observable.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [Fintype Mode] [inst : DecidableEq Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ),
  (∀ (k : Mode), 0 < β * ε k) →
    ∀ (i j : Mode),
      SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsSummable ε β
          (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Bosonic.create j) →
        1 - Complex.exp ↑(-ε i * β) ≠ 0 →
          SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsExpectation ε β
              (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Bosonic.create j) =
            (if i = j then 1 else 0) / (1 - Complex.exp ↑(-ε i * β))
name: SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsExpectation_annihilate_comp_create_eq
docString:

this statement can be reused by convergence-aware Wick data without hiding the analytic input.

statement:

∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (s : SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics)
  (energy : Config → ℝ) (β : ℝ) (n : ℕ)
  (C :
    Fin (2 * n) → SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (q : Fin (2 * n) → ℝ) (c : Fin (2 * n) → Fin (2 * n) → ℂ),
  (∀ (i : Fin (2 * n)),
      (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) (C i) = Complex.exp ↑(q i * -β) • C i) →
    (∀ (i j : Fin (2 * n)), i ≠ j → ScalarExchange.zetaCommutator (↑s.zetaInt) (C i) (C j) = c i j • LinearMap.id) →
      (∀ (i : Fin (2 * n)), 1 - ↑s.zetaInt * Complex.exp ↑(q i * β) ≠ 0) →
        SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (List.ofFn C).prod =
          ∑ pairing,
            Combinatorics.Pairing.weight s pairing *
              ∏ pr ∈ pairing.pairs, SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C pr.1 ∘ₗ C pr.2)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.BlochDeDominicis.finiteGibbsExpectation_prod_eq_sum_pairing
docString:
**The general finite-temperature Bloch–de Dominicis theorem.** The original linked-diagram
and finite-temperature pairing development is C. Bloch and C. de Dominicis, *Nuclear Physics*
**7**, 459–479 (1958),
[doi:10.1016/0029-5582(58)90285-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/0029-5582(58)90285-2).
For the unified bosonic/fermionic thermal Wick argument motivating this pairing formula, see M. Gaudin, *Nuclear
Physics* **15**, 89–91 (1960),
[doi:10.1016/0029-5582(60)90285-6](https://doi.org/10.1016/0029-5582(60)90285-6). This theorem is
the finite-Gibbs recursion specialization described above; it does not claim the infinite-volume
or interacting-state generality of the original diagrammatic development.

  (pairValue : Fin (2 * (2 * S.card + E)) → Fin (2 * (2 * S.card + E)) → ℂ)
  (localPairValue :
    (B : ↥d.vertexGraph.componentPartition.parts) →
      Fin (2 * (2 * (SecondQuantization.Common.interactionSector ↑B).card + d.externalPairCount B)) →
        Fin (2 * (2 * (SecondQuantization.Common.interactionSector ↑B).card + d.externalPairCount B)) → ℂ),
  (∀ (B : ↥d.vertexGraph.componentPartition.parts)
      (a b : Fin (2 * (2 * (SecondQuantization.Common.interactionSector ↑B).card + d.externalPairCount B))),
      pairValue (d.componentDiagramLeg B a) (d.componentDiagramLeg B b) = localPairValue B a b) →
    d.pairing.evaluation (Combinatorics.Pairing.weight s d.pairing) pairValue =
      ↑s.zetaInt ^ d.interComponentCrossingCount *
        ∏ B,
          (d.restrictComponent B).pairing.evaluation (Combinatorics.Pairing.weight s (d.restrictComponent B).pairing)
            (localPairValue B)

inter-component exchange weight and component-local pairing evaluations whenever the pair kernel is
local under the canonical component leg embeddings.

  (create annihilate :
    Mode → SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (leg : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticLocalLeg Mode) (τ : ℝ),
  (∀ (i : Mode),
      (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) (create i) = Complex.exp (↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • create i) →
    (∀ (i : Mode),
        (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) (annihilate i) =
          Complex.exp (-↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • annihilate i) →
      (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) (leg.operator create annihilate) =
        Complex.exp ↑(τ * SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticLocalLeg.energyShift ε leg) • leg.operator create annihilate

docString: A local quartic leg assembled from ladder eigenoperators evolves with its signed energy shift.

  (ext : SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram ExternalLabel InternalLabel n T)
  (vac : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram InternalLabel n (Finset.univ \ T)) (τ τ' : ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ)
  (hσ : StrictAnti (σ ∘ SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumSlot T))
  (pr : (vac.pairingInOrder (SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumOrder T)).NormalizedPair),
  let d := SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.ofSlotSplit ⋯ ext vac;
  have q :=
    (SecondQuantization.Common.orderedLegToDiagramLeg (Finset.univ \ T)

      (↑pr).1;
  d.mixedPairComponent τ τ' σ
      ((SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.slotSplitVacuumNormalizedPairEmbedding T ext vac τ τ' σ hσ) pr) =
    ⟨d.vertexGraph.componentBlock
        (SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumVertex (SecondQuantization.Common.vertexOfLeg q)),
      ⋯⟩

by the corresponding right-side quartic vertex.

statement:
∀ {ExternalLabel : Type u_1} {InternalLabel : Type u_2} {N : ℕ} {S T : Finset (Fin N)} {M : Type u_3}
  [inst : CommMonoid M] (h : T ⊆ S) (ext : SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram ExternalLabel InternalLabel N T)
  (vac : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram InternalLabel N (S \ T)),
  ext.IsExternallyConnected →
    ∀ (w : InternalLabel → M),
      ∏
          B ∈
            SecondQuantization.Common.vacuumComponentParts

∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config]
  (L : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (F : ℝ → SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (a b : ℝ),
  (∀ (k n : Config),
      IntervalIntegrable (fun σ => SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (F σ) k n) MeasureTheory.volume a b) →
    L ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.operatorIntervalIntegral F a b =
      SecondQuantization.Common.operatorIntervalIntegral (fun σ => L ∘ₗ F σ) a b
name: SecondQuantization.Common.comp_operatorIntervalIntegral
docString:
**Left-composition with a fixed operator commutes with `operatorIntervalIntegral`**:
`L ∘ (∫ F) = ∫ (L ∘ F)`, given interval-integrability of every matrix coefficient `F` contributes.
Both sides reduce, via `matrixCoeff_comp`/`matrixCoeff_operatorIntervalIntegral`, to the same
`∑ k, matrixCoeff L m k * ∫ σ, matrixCoeff (F σ) k n` vs. `∫ σ, ∑ k, matrixCoeff L m k *
matrixCoeff (F σ) k n` — the finite-sum/integral interchange `intervalIntegral.integral_finsetSum`
supplies, after pulling the constant `matrixCoeff L m k` in/out of each summand's integral
(`intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul`). Needed to move an already-evaluated interaction-picture
vertex factor past the ordered-simplex integral over the *remaining* Dyson coefficient.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (ζ : ℂ)
  (C1 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (l :
    List ((SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) × ℂ)),
  (∀ p ∈ l, ScalarExchange.zetaCommutator ζ C1 p.1 = p.2 • LinearMap.id) →
    C1 ∘ₗ (List.map Prod.fst l).prod =
      ScalarExchange.peelSumWithCoefficients ζ l + ζ ^ l.length • (List.map Prod.fst l).prod ∘ₗ C1
name: SecondQuantization.Common.comp_prod_eq_of_zetaCommutator
docString:
**Peeling `C₁` through an arbitrary-length product**: repeatedly rewriting `C₁Bⱼ` via each
pair's `ζ`-commutator coefficient and pushing `C₁` rightward, `C₁` lands at the very end having
picked up `ζ^{l.length}`.

∀ {Config : Type u_1} (energy : Config → ℝ) (τ q : ℝ)
  (C : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) C = Complex.exp ↑(q * τ) • C →
    SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy τ ∘ₗ C =
      Complex.exp ↑(q * τ) • C ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy τ
name: SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution_comp_eq_smul_comp_diagonalEvolution
docString:
**The KMS-type relation**: if a linear map `C` picks up an exponential eigenvalue-shift factor
`e^{qτ}` under `heisenbergEvolve` (as every `create`/`annihilate` operator does, with `q` the
eigenvalue shift `∓ε_i`), then `e^{τH₀}` and `C` satisfy `e^{τH₀} C = e^{qτ} C e^{τH₀}` — the exact
statistics-agnostic algebraic ingredient the finite-temperature Bloch–de Dominicis theorem's
KMS-rotation step needs (`ĉ_α e^{-βĤ} = e^{-βξ_α} e^{-βĤ} ĉ_α` in the project's physics reference
notes, `quantum-statistical-mechanics.tex`'s "product-of-KMS-state-and-ladder-op"), obtained purely
by rearranging the already-proved semigroup law and mutual inversion
(`diagonalEvolution_neg_comp`) — no new physical input beyond the eigenvalue-shift hypothesis
`hC`, and in particular no dependence on the concrete occupation-state type or exchange statistics.
Both `Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve_annihilate`/`_create` and
`Bosonic.imaginaryTimeEvolve_annihilate`/`_create` supply exactly this hypothesis (with
`q := -ε i`/`q := ε i` respectively), so this single `Common/` lemma gives the KMS relation for
`create`/`annihilate` in both statistics at once.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {Config : Type u_2} (energy : Config → ℝ) (ε : Mode → ℝ)
  (create annihilate :
    Mode → SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (support : Finset (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode))
  (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ),
  (∀ (τ : ℝ) (i : Mode),
      (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) (create i) = Complex.exp (↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • create i) →
    (∀ (τ : ℝ) (i : Mode),
        (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) (annihilate i) =
          Complex.exp (-↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • annihilate i) →
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ),
        SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff energy
            (SecondQuantization.Common.quarticInteractionOn support create annihilate g) n t =
          ∑ q,
            SecondQuantization.Common.quarticDysonSequenceCoeff ε g (fun i => ↑(q i)) t •
              SecondQuantization.Common.quarticVertexSequenceOperator create annihilate fun i => ↑(q i)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff_quarticInteractionOn_eq_sum
docString:
The finite-order Dyson coefficient of a finitely supported quartic interaction is the sum over
support-valued vertex sequences of their scalar ordered-simplex coefficients multiplying the
corresponding bare vertex products. This is statistics-independent once the ladder operators obey
the stated free imaginary-time eigenoperator laws.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {Config : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype Mode] (energy : Config → ℝ) (ε : Mode → ℝ)
  (create annihilate :
    Mode → SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ),
  (∀ (τ : ℝ) (i : Mode),
      (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) (create i) = Complex.exp (↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • create i) →
    (∀ (τ : ℝ) (i : Mode),
        (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) (annihilate i) =
          Complex.exp (-↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • annihilate i) →
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ),
        SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff energy (SecondQuantization.Common.quarticInteraction create annihilate g) n
            t =
          ∑ q,
            SecondQuantization.Common.quarticDysonSequenceCoeff ε g q t •
              SecondQuantization.Common.quarticVertexSequenceOperator create annihilate q
name: SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff_quarticInteraction_eq_sum
docString:
On a finite mode type, the quartic Dyson coefficient is the sum over all vertex-label
sequences of the statistics-independent scalar ordered-simplex coefficient times the bare vertex
product.

statement:

    -SecondQuantization.Common.operatorIntervalIntegral

∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ)
  (ζ c12 c13 c14 : ℂ)
  (C1 C2 C3 C4 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    C1 ∘ₗ C2 - ζ • C2 ∘ₗ C1 = c12 • LinearMap.id →
      C1 ∘ₗ C3 - ζ • C3 ∘ₗ C1 = c13 • LinearMap.id →
        C1 ∘ₗ C4 - ζ • C4 ∘ₗ C1 = c14 • LinearMap.id →
          1 - ζ ^ 3 * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β) ≠ 0 →
            SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ C2 ∘ₗ C3 ∘ₗ C4) =
              (c12 * SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C3 ∘ₗ C4) +
                    ζ * c13 * SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C2 ∘ₗ C4) +
                  ζ ^ 2 * c14 * SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C2 ∘ₗ C3)) /
                (1 - ζ ^ 3 * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β))

docString: The normalized 4-point first-operator reduction.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ)

  (C1 Cj : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    SecondQuantization.Common.exchangeCommutator s C1 Cj = c1j • LinearMap.id →
      1 - ↑s.zetaInt * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β) ≠ 0 →
        SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ Cj) =
          c1j / (1 - ↑s.zetaInt * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β))
name: SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation_comp_eq_div_of_exchangeCommutator
docString:
**The `Statistics`-indexed presentation**, in terms of `exchangeCommutator s` rather than a
raw `ζ : ℂ` bracket — the form callers already holding a `Statistics` value should reach for.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ) (ζ c1j : ℂ)
  (C1 Cj : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    ScalarExchange.zetaCommutator ζ C1 Cj = c1j • LinearMap.id →
      1 - ζ * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β) ≠ 0 →
        SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ Cj) = c1j / (1 - ζ * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β))
name: SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation_comp_eq_div_of_zetaCommutator
docString:
**The genuine normalized 2-point Bloch–de Dominicis value**: `⟨C₁Cⱼ⟩ = c₁ⱼ/(1 - ζw₁)`,
dividing the singleton-tail peel identity `(1 - ζw₁) Tr[e^{-βH₀}(C₁Cⱼ)] = c₁ⱼ Tr[e^{-βH₀}]` through
by the genuine (nonzero) partition function and by the (assumed nonzero) `1 - ζw₁` factor —
matching the physics reference notes' `⟨Ĉ₁Ĉⱼ⟩ = C_{1,j}/(1 - ζw₁)` letter-for-letter rather than
leaving it as an un-divided trace equation.

statement:

statement:

`Tr[e^{-βH₀}A] / Tr[e^{-βH₀}]`.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ)
  (ζ c12 c13 c14 : ℂ)
  (C1 C2 C3 C4 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    C1 ∘ₗ C2 - ζ • C2 ∘ₗ C1 = c12 • LinearMap.id →
      C1 ∘ₗ C3 - ζ • C3 ∘ₗ C1 = c13 • LinearMap.id →
        C1 ∘ₗ C4 - ζ • C4 ∘ₗ C1 = c14 • LinearMap.id →
          ζ ^ 2 = 1 →
            1 - ζ * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β) ≠ 0 →
              SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ C2 ∘ₗ C3 ∘ₗ C4) =
                SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ C2) *
                      SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C3 ∘ₗ C4) +
                    ζ * SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ C3) *
                      SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C2 ∘ₗ C4) +
                  SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ C4) *
                    SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C2 ∘ₗ C3)

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ) (ζ : ℂ)
  (C1 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (l :
    List ((SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) × ℂ)),
  (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    (∀ p ∈ l, ScalarExchange.zetaCommutator ζ C1 p.1 = p.2 • LinearMap.id) →
      1 - ζ ^ l.length * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β) ≠ 0 →
        SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ (List.map Prod.fst l).prod) =
          SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (ScalarExchange.peelSumWithCoefficients ζ l) /
            (1 - ζ ^ l.length * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β))
name: SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation_peel
docString: The normalized peel-first identity in the canonical finite Gibbs density state.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β : ℝ) (ζ : ℂ)

    ∑ j,

        SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (List.map Prod.fst (l.eraseIdx ↑j)).prod

  (support : Finset (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode))
  (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (τ : ℝ),
  (∀ (i : Mode),
      (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) (create i) = Complex.exp (↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • create i) →
    (∀ (i : Mode),
        (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) (annihilate i) =

      (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ)
          (SecondQuantization.Common.quarticInteractionOn support create annihilate g) =

            SecondQuantization.Common.quarticVertexOperator create annihilate ↑q

      (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) (create i) = Complex.exp (↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • create i) →

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config]
  (A B : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (m n : Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (A ∘ₗ B) m n =
    ∑ k, SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff A m k * SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff B k n
name: SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff_comp
docString:
**`matrixCoeff` under composition is ordinary matrix multiplication** on a finite
configuration type: `(AB)_{mn} = Σₖ A_{mk} B_{kn}`.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1}
  (A B : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (m n : Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (A ∘ₗ B) m n =
    ∑ k ∈ (B (SecondQuantization.Common.basisState n)).support,
      SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff A m k * SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff B k n
name: SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff_comp_support
docString:
**`matrixCoeff` under composition, as a sum over `B`'s finite support**:
`(AB)_{mn} = Σ_{k ∈ supp(B|n⟩)} A_{mk} B_{kn}`. This holds for arbitrary `Config`, because an
`AlgebraicFock Config` vector is finitely supported even when `Config` itself is infinite.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (energy : Config → ℝ) (β : ℝ) (m n : Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β)) m n =
    if m = n then SecondQuantization.Common.boltzmannWeight energy β m else 0
name: SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff_diagonalEvolution
docString: `diagonalEvolution` is diagonal with the complex Boltzmann weights.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (energy : Config → ℝ) (τ : ℝ)
  (A : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (m n : Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy τ ∘ₗ A) m n =
    Complex.exp ↑(τ * energy m) * SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff A m n
name: SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff_diagonalEvolution_comp
docString:
Left composition by a diagonal evolution rescales a matrix coefficient by the output
configuration's exponential weight.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (energy : Config → ℝ) (τ : ℝ) (m n : Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy τ) m n =
    if m = n then Complex.exp ↑(τ * energy n) else 0
name: SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff_diagonalEvolution_eq_ite
docString:
**`diagonalEvolution`'s matrix coefficients**: diagonal, `exp(τ · energy n)` on the diagonal
and `0` off it — the algebraic content of "`diagonalEvolution` acts on each basis state by a
scalar". Specialized to `energy := freeEigenvalue`/`fermionEnergy`, `τ := -β`, the same formula
provides the basis-diagonal Gibbs-weight coefficients.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (a : Config → ℂ) (m n : Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalOperator a) m n = if m = n then a n else 0
name: SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff_diagonalOperator
SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff_eq_ite_of_basisState_smul
docString:
**Matrix coefficients of a one-basis-state image.** If `A` sends `basisState n` to
`c • basisState k`, its `(m, n)` coefficient is `c` at `m = k` and `0` elsewhere.

name: SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff_ext
docString: **Two operators agreeing on every matrix coefficient are equal.**

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (energy : Config → ℝ) (τ : ℝ)
  (A : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (m n : Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff ((SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) A) m n =
    Complex.exp ↑(τ * (energy m - energy n)) * SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff A m n
name: SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff_heisenbergEvolve
docString:
**`heisenbergEvolve`'s matrix coefficients**: `A(τ)`'s `(m, n)` entry is `A`'s own `(m, n)`
entry, rescaled by `exp(τ(energy m - energy n))` — the interaction-picture matrix-coefficient
formula, for an arbitrary configuration type.

statement: ∀ {Config : Type u_1} (m n : Config), SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff LinearMap.id m n = if m = n then 1 else 0
name: SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff_id
docString: The identity operator has the Kronecker-delta matrix in the canonical basis.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (energy : Config → ℝ)
  (V : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) (τ : ℝ)
  (m n : Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (SecondQuantization.Common.interactionPicture energy V τ) m n =
    Complex.exp ↑(τ * (energy m - energy n)) * SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff V m n
name: SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff_interactionPicture
docString:
Matrix coefficients acquire the exponential of the free energy difference. No `Fintype`
assumption on `Config` is needed.

statement:

  (a b : ℝ) (m n : Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (SecondQuantization.Common.operatorIntervalIntegral F a b) m n =

name: SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff_operatorIntervalIntegral
docString:
**The matrix-coefficient formula**: `operatorIntervalIntegral`'s own matrix coefficients are
exactly the scalar interval integrals of `F`'s matrix coefficients.

  event ∈ SecondQuantization.Common.orderedTwoPointTimedEvents τ τ' σ →
    x ∈ SecondQuantization.Common.twoPointTimedEventAtomicLegs event →
      y ∈ SecondQuantization.Common.twoPointTimedEventAtomicLegs event →
        z ∈ SecondQuantization.Common.mixedTimeOrderedAtomicLegs τ τ' σ →
          z ∉ SecondQuantization.Common.twoPointTimedEventAtomicLegs event →
            (SecondQuantization.Common.mixedTimeOrderedAtomicLegPosition τ τ' σ x <
                SecondQuantization.Common.mixedTimeOrderedAtomicLegPosition τ τ' σ z) =

                SecondQuantization.Common.mixedTimeOrderedAtomicLegPosition τ τ' σ z)

name: SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_rotate
docString:
**The KMS-type trace rotation**: `Tr[e^{-βH₀} (A C)] = e^{qβ} Tr[e^{-βH₀} (C A)]`, for any
operator `A` and any operator `C` with eigenvalue-shift `q` under `heisenbergEvolve`. Combines
`traceFock_comp_comm` (cyclicity) with `comp_diagonalEvolution_eq_smul_diagonalEvolution_comp` (the
KMS-type relation) exactly as the physics reference notes' `⟨Ĉ₂⋯Ĉ_{2n}Ĉ₁⟩ = w₁⟨Ĉ₁Ĉ₂⋯Ĉ_{2n}⟩` step
does.

docString: The trace of the free diagonal evolution is the complex Boltzmann weight sum.

    (Summable fun n => SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff B n n) →

  Summable
      (Function.uncurry fun n k =>
        SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff A n k * SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff B k n) →
    SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace (A ∘ₗ B) = SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace (B ∘ₗ A)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace_comp_comm
docString:
**Cyclicity under a two-operator swap**, assuming absolute double summability:
`Tr'[AB] = Tr'[BA]`.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ) (ζ : ℂ)
  (C1 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (l :
    List ((SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) × ℂ)),
  (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    (∀ p ∈ l, ScalarExchange.zetaCommutator ζ C1 p.1 = p.2 • LinearMap.id) →
      (Summable fun n =>
          SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff
            (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ ScalarExchange.peelSumWithCoefficients ζ l) n
            n) →
        Summable
            (Function.uncurry fun n k =>
              SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff
                  (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ (List.map Prod.fst l).prod) n k *
                SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff C1 k n) →
          (1 - ζ ^ l.length * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β)) *
              SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace
                (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ C1 ∘ₗ (List.map Prod.fst l).prod) =
            SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace
              (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ ScalarExchange.peelSumWithCoefficients ζ l)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace_diagonalEvolution_comp_peel
docString:
**The `tsum` trace-level peel-first identity**: the `[Fintype Config]`-free analogue of
`traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_peel`, given the same `ζ`-commutator and KMS eigenvalue-shift
hypotheses plus explicit summability of `ScalarExchange.peelSumWithCoefficients`'s own diagonal series (`hPeel`) and of the
rotation's double series (`hRotate`). Summability of the rotated tail's diagonal series (`n ↦
(e^{-βH₀}(B₁⋯Bₖ)C₁)ₙₙ`) is *not* a separate hypothesis — it follows from `hRotate` alone via
`summable_matrixCoeff_diag_comp_of_summable_uncurry`.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q : ℝ)
  (A C : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) C = Complex.exp ↑(q * -β) • C →
    Summable
        (Function.uncurry fun n k =>
          SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ A) n k *
            SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff C k n) →
      SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ A ∘ₗ C) =
        Complex.exp ↑(q * β) •
          SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ C ∘ₗ A)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace_diagonalEvolution_comp_rotate
docString:
**The `tsum` KMS-type trace rotation**: the `[Fintype Config]`-free analogue of
`traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_rotate`, built from `Common.tsumTrace_comp_comm` instead of
`traceFock_comp_comm`. This lets the rotation step operate on a genuine bosonic occupation type at
the cost of the explicit double-summability hypothesis `h`, unlike the `[Fintype Config]` case
where summability is automatic.

∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hsum : QuantumTheory.PurePointGibbsSummable (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β) (n : ℕ)
  (C : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode)
  (l : List (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode)),
  l.length = 2 * n + 1 →
    1 + SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.gibbsFactor ε β C ≠ 0 →
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum (C :: l) =
        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.gibbsFactor ε β C /
            (1 + SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.gibbsFactor ε β C) *
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedFreeGibbsDensityOperator ε β hsum).expectation
            (ScalarExchange.peelSum SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.operator
              SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.anticommutatorValue (-1) C l)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation_cons_eq_gibbsRatio_mul_peel
docString:
For an odd tail, completed CAR exchange followed by KMS rotation solves the wrapped term.
The coefficient `g / (1 + g)` is the Fermi thermal factor attached to the leading ladder.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hsum : QuantumTheory.PurePointGibbsSummable (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β)
  (C₁ : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode)
  (l : List (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode)),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum (C₁ :: l) =
    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedFreeGibbsDensityOperator ε β hsum).expectation
        (ScalarExchange.peelSum SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.operator
          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.anticommutatorValue (-1) C₁ l) +
      (-1) ^ l.length *
        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum (l ++ [C₁])
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation_cons_eq_peel_add_rotated
docString: Expectation-level exchange formula before the KMS rotation of the final term.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hsum : QuantumTheory.PurePointGibbsSummable (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β) (n : ℕ)
  (C : Fin (2 * n) → SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsAdmissible ε β n C →
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum (List.ofFn C) =
      ∑ pairing,
        Combinatorics.Pairing.weight SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.fermion pairing *
          ∏ pr ∈ pairing.pairs,
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum [C pr.1, C pr.2]
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation_eq_sum_pairing
docString:
Completed free-fermion Bloch--de Dominicis expansion obtained by feeding the completed Gibbs
recursion data into the common pairing induction.

statement:

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hsum : QuantumTheory.PurePointGibbsSummable (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β)
  (C : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode)

    ↥(SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedFockSpace Mode) →L[ℂ]
      ↥(SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedFockSpace Mode)),
  (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedFreeGibbsDensityOperator ε β hsum).expectation (C.operator ∘SL A) =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.gibbsFactor ε β C *
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedFreeGibbsDensityOperator ε β hsum).expectation (A ∘SL C.operator)

docString:
Completed free-Gibbs KMS rotation for one thermal ladder and an arbitrary bounded operator:
`⟨C A⟩β = gβ(C) ⟨A C⟩β`.  The scalar `gβ(C)` is the same factor appearing in

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hsum : QuantumTheory.PurePointGibbsSummable (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β)
  (C D : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode),
  1 + SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.gibbsFactor ε β C ≠ 0 →
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum [C, D] =
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.gibbsFactor ε β C /
          (1 + SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.gibbsFactor ε β C) *
        C.anticommutatorValue D

by the same Gibbs ratio that solves the odd-tail KMS equation.

docString:
The ambient free-Gibbs pair contraction restricts to the standalone component pair contraction
under the canonical mixed-position embedding.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {E n : ℕ}
  (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram Mode E n) (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram.fixedTimeAmplitude_eq_componentExternalOrderSign_mul_prod_components
docString:
A fixed-time external-insertion amplitude is the fixed external regrouping sign times the
product of the standalone fixed-time amplitudes of all full connected components.

The arbitrary-external fermionic Dyson fixed-time integrand is measurable

The residual mixed-order inter-component crossing parity is the total inversion parity of the
canonical mixed component-position shuffle.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {E n : ℕ}
  (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram Mode E n) (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ),
  ∏ pr ∈ (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.pairingInMixedOrder d externalTime σ).pairs,
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalInsertionMixedTimeOrderedAtomicPairValue ε β d.externalLabel externalTime
        d.vertexLabelSequence σ pr.1 pr.2 =
    ∏ B,
      ∏
        pr ∈
          (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.pairingInMixedOrder (d.componentWickDiagram B)
              (d.componentExternalTime externalTime B) (d.componentInteractionTime σ B)).pairs,
        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalInsertionMixedTimeOrderedAtomicPairValue ε β
          (d.componentWickDiagram B).externalLabel (d.componentExternalTime externalTime B)
          (d.componentWickDiagram B).vertexLabelSequence (d.componentInteractionTime σ B) pr.1 pr.2
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram.mixedPairContractionProduct_eq_prod_components
docString:
The product of concrete mixed-time free-Gibbs pair contractions factors over connected
components.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {E n : ℕ}
  (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram Mode E n) (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ),
  d.mixedPairingValue ε β externalTime σ =
    ↑SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.fermion.zetaInt ^
        (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.pairingInMixedOrder d externalTime
              σ).interComponentCrossingCount
          (d.componentMixedPairEquiv externalTime σ) *
      ∏ B,
        (d.componentWickDiagram B).mixedPairingValue ε β (d.componentExternalTime externalTime B)
          (d.componentInteractionTime σ B)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram.mixedPairingValue_eq_inter_mul_prod_components
docString:
The concrete mixed pairing evaluation factors into the residual mixed inter-component fermionic
sign and the standalone mixed pairing values of all connected components.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {E n : ℕ} (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram Mode E n)

      (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.externalPairCount d B)

docString:
The timed field attached to a component-local canonical leg is exactly the ambient timed field
on the corresponding canonical leg.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {E n : ℕ}
  (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram Mode E n) (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)

    d.dysonAmplitude ε β g externalTime
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram.orderedSimplexIntegral_dysonFixedTimeAmplitude
docString: Integrating the Dyson-signed fixed-time amplitude is the integrated Dyson amplitude.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {E n : ℕ} (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram Mode E n)
  (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ),
  (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.pairingInMixedOrder d externalTime σ).crossingCount =

        (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.pairingInMixedOrder (d.componentWickDiagram B)
            (d.componentExternalTime externalTime B) (d.componentInteractionTime σ B)).crossingCount +
      (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.pairingInMixedOrder d externalTime
            σ).interComponentCrossingCount
        (d.componentMixedPairEquiv externalTime σ)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram.pairingInMixedOrder_crossingCount_eq_sum_components_add_inter
docString:
The mixed-order crossing count is the sum of component-local mixed crossing counts and
the residual crossings between distinct components.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {E n : ℕ} (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram Mode E n)
  (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ)

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram.pairingInMixedOrder_partner_componentMixedPosition
docString:
The ambient mixed-order pairing partner of an embedded component position is the embedding of
the component mixed-order pairing partner.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {E n : ℕ} (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram Mode E n)
  (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ) (leg : SecondQuantization.Common.OrderedExternalInsertionLeg E n),

      (SecondQuantization.Common.externalInsertionMixedTimeOrderedAtomicLegPosition externalTime σ leg) =

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram.pairingInMixedOrder_partner_legPosition
docString:
The mixed-order partner of the position selected by a canonical leg is the mixed position of
that leg's diagram partner.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {E n : ℕ} (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram Mode E n)
  (s : SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics) (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ),
  Combinatorics.Pairing.weight s
      (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.pairingInMixedOrder d externalTime σ) =
    ↑s.zetaInt ^
        (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.pairingInMixedOrder d externalTime
              σ).interComponentCrossingCount
          (d.componentMixedPairEquiv externalTime σ) *
      ∏ B,
        Combinatorics.Pairing.weight s
          (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.pairingInMixedOrder (d.componentWickDiagram B)
            (d.componentExternalTime externalTime B) (d.componentInteractionTime σ B))

docString:
The exchange-statistics weight of the mixed-order pairing factors into a residual
inter-component weight and the standalone mixed-order component weights.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {E n : ℕ} (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram Mode E n)
  (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ)
  (blockOrder :
    ↥(SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.vertexGraph d).componentPartition.parts ≃
      Fin (Fintype.card ↥(SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.vertexGraph d).componentPartition.parts)),
  ↑↑(Equiv.Perm.sign (d.relativeComponentShuffle externalTime σ)) =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.componentExternalOrderSign d blockOrder *
      ↑SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.fermion.zetaInt ^ d.mixedInterComponentCrossingCount externalTime σ
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram.relativeComponentShuffleSign_eq_external_mul_mixedInter
docString:
The relative permutation between fixed and mixed component shuffles carries exactly the fixed
external regrouping sign and the residual mixed inter-component crossing sign.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {E n : ℕ}
  (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram Mode E n) (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ)
  (blockOrder :
    ↥(SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.vertexGraph d).componentPartition.parts ≃
      Fin (Fintype.card ↥(SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.vertexGraph d).componentPartition.parts)),
  ↑↑(Equiv.Perm.sign (d.relativeComponentShuffle externalTime σ)) * d.mixedPairingValue ε β externalTime σ =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.componentExternalOrderSign d blockOrder *
      ∏ B,
        (d.componentWickDiagram B).mixedPairingValue ε β (d.componentExternalTime externalTime B)
          (d.componentInteractionTime σ B)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram.relativeComponentShuffleSign_mul_mixedPairingValue_eq_componentExternalOrderSign_mul_prod_components
docString:
Multiplying the mixed pairing value by the sign that carries fixed component-leg order to
mixed-time component-leg order leaves the fixed external-component sign times the component-local
mixed pairing values. This is a pairing-level identity; it does not assert factorization of the
full fixed-time amplitude.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {E n : ℕ} (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram Mode E n)
  (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ),
  Equiv.Perm.sign (d.relativeComponentShuffle externalTime σ) =
    Equiv.Perm.sign (SecondQuantization.Common.externalInsertionStandardToMixedAtomicPositionEquiv externalTime σ) *
      ∏ B,
        Equiv.Perm.sign
          (SecondQuantization.Common.externalInsertionStandardToMixedAtomicPositionEquiv
            (d.componentExternalTime externalTime B) (d.componentInteractionTime σ B))
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram.relativeComponentShuffle_sign_eq_mixedAtomic_mul_prod_components
docString:
The relative component shuffle sign is the ambient mixed-time ordering sign times the product
of the component-local mixed-time ordering signs. This is the final permutation-sign bridge needed
to turn mixed-pairing factorization into a fixed-time amplitude factorization.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {E n : ℕ}
  (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram Mode E n) (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ)
  (blockOrder :
    ↥(SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.vertexGraph d).componentPartition.parts ≃
      Fin (Fintype.card ↥(SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.vertexGraph d).componentPartition.parts)),
  ∑ shuffle,
      d.orderedDysonAmplitude ε β g externalTime
        (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.assembleInteractionOrder d
          (SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.canonicalComponentInteractionOrders d) shuffle) =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.componentExternalOrderSign d blockOrder *
      ∏ B, (d.componentWickDiagram B).dysonAmplitude ε β g (d.componentExternalTime externalTime B)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram.sum_componentInteractionOrderShuffle_orderedDysonAmplitude_eq_componentExternalOrderSign_mul_prod_components
docString:
The interaction-order shuffle orbit of an arbitrary external-insertion diagram factors into
the fixed external regrouping sign times the product of the standalone component amplitudes.

statement:

  [inst_2 : AddCommGroup 𝓗₁] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ 𝓗₁] (q : ℂ) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] 𝓗₁ →ₗ[ℂ] 𝓗₁) (f : Test),

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (𝓗₁ : Type u_2)
  [inst_2 : AddCommGroup 𝓗₁] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ 𝓗₁] (h : 𝓗₁ →ₗ[ℂ] 𝓗₁) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] 𝓗₁ →ₗ[ℂ] 𝓗₁)
  (m : 𝓗₁ →ₗ[ℂ] 𝓗₁) (f : Test),
  ⁅SecondQuantization.Fermionic.AlgebraicFock.dGamma 𝓗₁ h,
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Field.manyBodyLocalizedQuantity 𝓗₁ M m) f⁆ =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.AlgebraicFock.dGamma 𝓗₁ (ConservationLaw.transportCommutator 𝓗₁ h M m f) +
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.AlgebraicFock.dGamma 𝓗₁ (ConservationLaw.sourceCommutator 𝓗₁ h M m f)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Field.dGamma_lie_manyBodyLocalizedQuantity
docString: Second quantization preserves the generalized balance decomposition.

  (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Field.l2ChargeDensity μ q) f =
    q •
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.AlgebraicFock.dGamma (L2Multiplication.ComplexL2 μ)
        ↑(L2Multiplication.multiplicationOperator μ f)

docString:
On the one-particle sector, the second-quantized `L²` charge density is exactly the
charge-scaled canonical bounded multiplication operator.

The signed pointwise amplitude is the external ordering sign times the product of all signed
component-local fixed-time values.

statement:

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {n : ℕ} {i j : Mode}

      eta lowerEnergy upperEnergy occupation →
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Transport.finiteStaticKuboBastinCurrentCurrentResponse system data geometry direction K
        q eta =
      ↑convention.volume * -↑eta *
          QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedTracedBastinEnergyIntegral (↑system.hamiltonian)
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)

          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalContact geometry direction (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)

∀ {Site : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {Ω : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_4} [inst : LinearOrder Site] [inst_1 : Fintype Site]

  (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble) (hbar : ℝ) (hbar_pos : 0 < hbar)
  (spectralData :
    (ω : Ω) → QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.PurePointLehmannData (ensemble.configurationSystem hbar hbar_pos ω) ι)
  (convention : QuantumTheory.Transport.PositiveVolume)
  (geometry : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LatticeGeometry Site E) (direction : E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ)
  (K : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LocallyFiniteHopping Site) (q eta lowerEnergy upperEnergy : ℝ)
  (occupation : ℝ → ℂ),
  (∀ (ω : Ω),
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Transport.FiniteStaticPeierlsWardIdentity convention
        (ensemble.configurationSystem hbar hbar_pos ω) (spectralData ω) geometry direction K q eta lowerEnergy
        upperEnergy occupation) →
    0 < eta →
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Transport.finiteDisorderAveragedStaticConductivity ensemble hbar hbar_pos
          spectralData convention geometry direction K q eta =
        ensemble.average fun ω =>
          QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedBastinSpectralEnergyIntegral (ensemble.configurationSystem hbar hbar_pos ω)
            (spectralData ω)
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction
              (↑(ensemble.configurationSystem hbar hbar_pos ω).hbar) (↑q) K)
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction
              (↑(ensemble.configurationSystem hbar hbar_pos ω).hbar) (↑q) K)
            (QuantumTheory.Transport.kuboBastinEnergyBroadening (ensemble.configurationSystem hbar hbar_pos ω).hbar eta)
            lowerEnergy upperEnergy occupation

  (K : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LocallyFiniteHopping Site),
  K.HasHermitianAmplitudes →
    ∀ (q ω η T : ℝ) {β M : ℝ},
      0 ≤ M →
        (∀ s ∈ Set.Icc 0 β,
            ‖QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.adiabaticCosineSource ω η T)
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K))
                  s‖ ≤
              M) →
          T ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
            IntervalIntegrable
                (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.adiabaticCosineSource ω η T)
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K)))
                MeasureTheory.volume 0 T →
              HasDerivAt
                (fun lam =>
                  QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.affinePerturbedExpectation system expectation
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation
                      (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.adiabaticCosineSource ω η T)
                      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                        (↑q) K))
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K)
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalContact geometry direction (↑system.hbar)

                0

∀ {Site : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [inst : LinearOrder Site] [inst_1 : Fintype Site] [inst_2 : AddCommGroup E]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℝ E]
  (system :
    QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.FiniteLatticeHilbertFock Site))
  (expectation :
    QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.NormalizedExpectation
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.FiniteLatticeHilbertFock Site))
  (f : ℝ → ℝ) (geometry : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LatticeGeometry Site E) (direction : E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ)
  (K : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LocallyFiniteHopping Site),
  K.HasHermitianAmplitudes →
    ∀ (q : ℝ) {β M t : ℝ},
      0 ≤ M →
        (∀ s ∈ Set.Icc 0 β,
            ‖QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K))
                  s‖ ≤
              M) →
          t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
            IntervalIntegrable
                (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K)))
                MeasureTheory.volume 0 t →
              HasDerivAt
                (fun lam =>
                  QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.affinePerturbedExpectation system expectation
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f
                      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                        (↑q) K))
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K)
                    (↑(f t) •
                      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalContact geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                        (↑q) K)
                    lam t)
                ((∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..t,
                    ↑(f s) *
                      QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.retardedSusceptibility system expectation
                        (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction
                          (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)
                        (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction
                          (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)
                        t s) +
                  expectation.toContinuousLinearMap
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system
                      (↑(f t) •
                        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalContact geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                          (↑q) K)
                      t))
                0

charge rather than supplied externally.

  (geometry : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LatticeGeometry Site E) (direction : E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ)
  (K : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LocallyFiniteHopping Site) (q ω η : ℝ),
  0 < η →
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Transport.infiniteTimeAdiabaticDirectionalCoefficient system
        (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.purePointNormalizedExpectation system data) geometry direction K q ω η =
      ∑ mn,
          QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.lehmannTerm system.hbar ω η (data.energy mn.1 - data.energy mn.2)
            (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.purePointTransitionWeight system data
              (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)
              (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)
              mn) +
        (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.purePointNormalizedExpectation system data).toContinuousLinearMap
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalContact geometry direction (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Transport.infiniteTimeAdiabaticDirectionalCoefficient_purePoint_eq_finite_sum
docString:
The full fixed-rate directional coefficient is the finite Lehmann sum plus the explicit
geometric Peierls contact expectation.

  (K : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LocallyFiniteHopping Site) (q ω η : ℝ),
  0 < η →
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Transport.infiniteTimeAdiabaticDirectionalConductivity volume system
        (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.purePointNormalizedExpectation system data) geometry direction K q ω η =
      (∑ mn,
            QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.lehmannTerm system.hbar ω η (data.energy mn.1 - data.energy mn.2)

            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalContact geometry direction (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)) *
        QuantumTheory.Transport.finiteVolumeConductivityNormalization volume ω η

statement:
∀ (omega eta : ℝ),
  eta ≠ 0 →
    QuantumTheory.Transport.finiteConductivityTableValue SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Validation.twoSiteDimerUnitVolume
        1 omega eta SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Validation.twoSiteDimerGroundStateConductivityTable =
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Validation.twoSiteDimerComplexRate omega eta *
        (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Validation.twoSiteDimerFrequencyDenominator omega eta)⁻¹
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Validation.twoSiteDimerGroundState_conductivity_frequency
docString:
Closed unit-volume finite-rate electrical conductivity of the unit-hopping dimer:

`σ(ω,η) = (η - iω) / ((η - iω)² + 4)`.

The proof keeps the Lehmann current response, Peierls contact `-1`, and electric-field
normalization as the existing public definitions and simplifies them only at the final scalar step.

statement:
QuantumTheory.Transport.finiteConductivityTableValue SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Validation.twoSiteDimerUnitVolume 1 0
    1 SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Validation.twoSiteDimerGroundStateConductivityTable =
  1 / 5
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Validation.twoSiteDimerGroundState_conductivity_zero_one
docString:
First exact end-to-end scalar electrical-conductivity benchmark:

`current-current = 4/5`, `contact = -1`, and the unit-volume electric-field normalization is `-1`,
so the fixed-rate conductivity at `ℏ = 1`, `ω = 0`, `η = 1` is exactly `1/5`.

∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (i : Mode) (n : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Occupation Mode),
  (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i) (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.basisState n) =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilateBasis i n
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate_basisState

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (i : Mode) (n : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Occupation Mode),
  (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i) (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.basisState n) =
    (if i ∈ n then ↑(SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionSign i n) else 0) •
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.basisState (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.removeOccupation i n)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate_basisState_eq
docString:
Uniform basis-state action of fermionic annihilation, with the empty-mode case absorbed into
the scalar coefficient.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] {i : Mode} {n : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Occupation Mode},
  i ∈ n →
    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i) (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.basisState n) =
      ↑(SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionSign i n) •
        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.basisState (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.removeOccupation i n)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate_basisState_of_mem
docString:
**Annihilation lowers the occupation.** Annihilating a particle in an occupied mode `i`
produces (up to the sign `fermionSign i n`) the basis state of `n` with `i` newly vacated — one
fewer particle than `n` (`particleNumber_removeOccupation_of_mem`).

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] {i : Mode} {n : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Occupation Mode},
  i ∉ n → (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i) (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.basisState n) = 0
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate_basisState_of_not_mem
docString: **The empty mode cannot be annihilated.**

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (i : Mode),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i +
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i =
    LinearMap.id
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate_comp_create_add_create_comp_annihilate
docString:
**`cᵢ cᵢ† + cᵢ† cᵢ = id`**, CAR's anticommutation relation rearranged: `cᵢ cᵢ† = id - Nᵢ`
together with `Nᵢ = cᵢ† cᵢ` by definition.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (i : Mode),
  (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i) ∘ₗ
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate_comp_create_comp_self
docString:
**`cᵢ cᵢ†` is idempotent**: `(cᵢ cᵢ†)(cᵢ cᵢ†) = cᵢ cᵢ†`, from `cᵢ cᵢ† = id - Nᵢ`
(`annihilate_comp_create_self`) and `Nᵢ`'s idempotency.

statement:

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate_comp_create_self
docString: **`c_i c_i† = id - N_i`**, an instance of `Common.annihilate_comp_create_self`.

**`annihilate i` carries particle-number charge `-1`**: it only ever connects a basis state
`m` to a basis state `n` with one fewer particle, `particleNumber m = particleNumber
n - 1`.

a basis state `n` with one more particle, `particleNumber m = particleNumber n +

`Common.continuous_matrixCoeff_interactionPicture`,
`Common.continuous_matrixCoeff_dysonCoeff`, and `Common.matrixCoeff_comp`; it is retained
independently of the quartic specialization below for downstream arguments that need continuity
of an interaction-picture operator composed with a Dyson coefficient.

  Continuous fun τ =>
    SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff
      (SecondQuantization.Common.quarticVertexSequenceInteractionPicture (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε)
        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate n q τ)

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.continuous_matrixCoeff_quarticVertexSequenceInteractionPicture
docString:
**Joint continuity, in the full time vector `τ`, of a matrix coefficient of
`Common.quarticVertexSequenceInteractionPicture`** — by induction on `n`: the base case is constant (`n = 0` gives `LinearMap.id`); the successor case's matrix coefficient is a finite sum of products of a
single-coordinate `Complex.exp` factor (`Common.continuous_matrixCoeff_interactionPicture`,
precomposed with the coordinate-`0` projection) and the inductive hypothesis (precomposed with the
"tail" projection `fun i => τ i.succ`). `[Fintype Mode]` is genuinely used (for the finite sum
`Common.matrixCoeff_comp` needs), just not in the statement itself — the linter can't see that.

  SecondQuantization.Common.dysonTraceVertexMoment (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β V S =
    ↑S.card.factorial *
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.freeGibbsDensityOperator ε β).expectation
        (SecondQuantization.Common.finiteHilbertOperatorAlgEquiv
          (SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) V S.card β))

docString:
The Common finite-configuration Dyson moment is the factorial times the fermionic free Gibbs
density-state expectation of the bare Dyson coefficient.

      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) S =

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {α : Type u_2} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)

  SecondQuantization.Common.dysonTraceVertexMoment (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) S =
    ↑S.card.factorial * (-1) ^ S.card *

              SecondQuantization.Fermionic.flatVertexLegPairingEvaluation ε β q τ pairing

docString:
Reindex the integrated arbitrary-external Dyson coefficient by the externally supported
interaction slots and the vacuum-free external / quartic diagram pair. Only the external
factor carries the fixed-label constraint.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {E : ℕ} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ)
  (externalLabel : Fin (2 * E) → SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalFieldLabel Mode) (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ)
  (n : ℕ),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalInsertionDysonCoefficient ε β g externalLabel externalTime n =
    ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
      ∑ T ∈ Finset.powersetCard m Finset.univ,
        ∑ p,
          if (↑p.1).externalLabel = externalLabel then
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram.dysonAmplitude
              (↑((SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.externalSupportFiberEquiv ⋯).symm p)) ε β g
              externalTime
          else 0
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalInsertionDysonCoefficient_eq_sum_powersetCard_externalSupportFiber
docString:
Group the external-support fibers by their number of interaction vertices.

This is the fixed-external coefficient in the cardinality coordinates needed for the binary
external/vacuum slot-shuffle decomposition. No amplitude product is asserted here.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {E : ℕ} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ)
  (externalLabel : Fin (2 * E) → SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalFieldLabel Mode) (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ)
  (m k : ℕ),
  (∑ T ∈ Finset.powersetCard m Finset.univ,
      ∑ p,
        if (↑p.1).externalLabel = externalLabel then
          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram.dysonAmplitude
            (↑((SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.externalSupportFiberEquiv ⋯).symm p)) ε β g
            externalTime
        else 0) =
    ∑ shuffle,
      ∑ q,
        have d :=
          ↑((SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.externalSupportFiberEquiv ⋯).symm
              ((SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.standardizedSupportFiberDataEquiv shuffle).symm q));
        if d.externalLabel = externalLabel then d.dysonAmplitude ε β g externalTime else 0
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalInsertionDysonCoefficient_powersetCard_eq_sum_standardizedSupportShuffle
docString:
Fixing external order `m` and vacuum order `k`, the integrated Dyson-amplitude
support fibers can be summed in standard coordinates independent of the shuffle.

The external-label constraint and the full integrated amplitude are retained; identifying
the shuffle sum with a product of separate integrals is the subsequent analytic step.

relabeling of atomic legs, with both times and field labels pulled back along the

  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalInsertionMixedTimeOrderedAtomicPairValue ε β externalLabel externalTime q σ
      (SecondQuantization.Common.externalInsertionMixedTimeOrderedAtomicLegPosition externalTime σ
        (Sum.inr
          (⟨((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv n) a).1, ⋯⟩,
            ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv n) a).2)))
      (SecondQuantization.Common.externalInsertionMixedTimeOrderedAtomicLegPosition externalTime σ
        (Sum.inr

arbitrary-external mixed-time leg order agrees with the canonical vacuum Dyson

the orientation of an ambient normalized pair after an external/vacuum shuffle.

  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalInsertionMixedTimeOrderedAtomicPairValue ε β externalLabel externalTime q σ

          (Sum.inr

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ),
  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (i j : Mode) (τ τ' : ℝ) (m k : ℕ),
      ∑ T, ∑ p, (↑((SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fixedExternalFiberEquiv ↑T).symm p)).dysonAmplitude ε β g τ τ' =
        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.connectedTwoPointDysonCoefficient ε β g i j τ τ' m *

            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) k

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {n : ℕ} {i j : Mode} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (T : Finset (Fin n))
  (ext : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.FixedExternalTwoPointWickDiagramOn Mode n T i j),
  SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.IsExternallyConnected ↑ext →
    ∀ (vac : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram Mode n (Finset.univ \ T)) (τ τ' : ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ),
      StrictAnti (σ ∘ SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumSlot T) →
        have d := SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fixedExternalOfSlotSplit T ext vac;
        (SecondQuantization.Common.vacuumComponentParts (SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.vertexGraph ↑d)).prod
            (d.mixedComponentDysonFixedTimeValue ε β g τ τ' σ) =
          (-1) ^ (Finset.univ \ T).card * SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.vertexWeight vac g *
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram.contractionIntegrand ε β vac
              (SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumOrder T) (σ ∘ SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumSlot T)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fixedExternalOfSlotSplit_prod_vacuumDysonFixedTimeValue_eq_quarticIntegrand
docString:
For an externally connected left piece and strictly decreasing inherited vacuum times, the
complete product of ambient vacuum-component Dyson fixed-time values is exactly the standalone
fixed-order quartic vacuum integrand, including its Dyson sign and vertex-weight prefactor.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {i j : Mode} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ),
  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (τ τ' : ℝ) {m k : ℕ}
      (shuffle : Combinatorics.SlotShuffle m k)
      (ext : { d // SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.IsExternallyConnected ↑d })
      (x : SecondQuantization.Common.OrderedQuarticDiagramData (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode) k),
      have p := (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fixedExternalShuffleFiberDataEquiv shuffle).symm (ext, x);
      have d := (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fixedExternalFiberEquiv shuffle.leftSlots).symm p;
      (↑d).dysonAmplitude ε β g τ τ' =
        intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral (m + k) β
          (shuffle.integrand (fun σ => (↑ext).dysonFixedTimeAmplitude ε β g τ τ' σ)
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedVacuumDysonIntegrand ε β g x))
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fixedExternalShuffleFiber_dysonAmplitude_eq_orderedSimplexIntegral
docString: **One fixed shuffle fiber is exactly the corresponding binary shuffled product integral.**

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {n : ℕ} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
